ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: This program is part of the Ophthalmology TA. It is a biologic fusion of proteins targeting VEGF-A, VEGF-B, PlGF, Ang-2 and IL-6.
TARGET_RATIONALE: VEGF, Ang-2, and IL-6 have been clinically validated as key targets in the treatment of Choroidal and Retinal Vascular Diseases, playing crucial roles in driving angiogenesis, vascular leakage, and inflammation. Despite current standard of care treatments involving intravitreal anti-VEGF and combined anti-VEGF+Ang-2 injections, there remains a significant unmet medical need. This is evidenced by the fact that 30-65% of Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) patients and 10-15% of wet Age-related Macular Degeneration (wAMD) patients are suboptimal responders to these therapies.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: This program is part of the Ophthalmology TA. It is a gene therapy (AAV) targeting VEGF-A, VEGF-B, PlGF, Ang-2 and IL-6.
TARGET_RATIONALE: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) represents a significant unmet medical need, affecting large patient populations with approximately 10-15% of cases proving refractory to current standard of care treatments. The disease is characterized by pathological neovascularization and vascular leakage, processes mediated by multiple angiogenic signaling factors including VEGF, Ang2, and IL-6, with ocular inflammation further driven by IL-6 signaling from the NLRP3 inflammasome.  The primary objective of this project is to develop a first-in-class (FIC) therapeutic approach that delivers a one-time, multi-targeting treatment utilizing AAV-mediated gene therapy to achieve durable suppression of VEGF, Ang2, and IL-6 signaling pathways. This innovative strategy aims to address the limitations of current therapies by providing sustained therapeutic benefit from a single administration, with the potential for expansion into multiple ophthalmologic indications beyond nAMD

PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_DESC: LC81687 - STAT6 sm degrader - Next Generation
TARGET_RATIONALE: IL-4 and IL-13 are dominant cytokines in Type 2 biology, driving many allergic diseases, and utilize JAK1 and STAT6 for activation and signalling. STAT6, however, is a transcription factor and the only STAT family member specifically involved in the IL-4/IL-13 signalling pathway. The IL-4/IL-13 pathway has been clinically credentialed in several Type 2 diseases e.g. Atopic Dermatitis, Asthma and Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps. The objective of the project is to develop a next generation oral STAT6-selective protein degrader. This would potentialy have similar  efficacy to biologics, but with more selectivity than JAK inhibitors, for therapeutic use in Type 2/TH2-mediated inflammatory disease. Next Generation molecules in-licensed from Nurix as part of STAT6 in-licensing agreement with all subsequent work to be done by Sanofi. ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The ST2 x TACI bispecific aims for aims for combined blockade of ST2, APRIL and BAFF via a hybrid containing a TACI fusion protein and an anti-ST2 moiety. It is expected to achieve effective disruption of immune priming pathways and epithelial alarmin response in severe asthma. IL-33 (via ST2 receptor binding on target cells) and activated mast cells (via mediator release) activate innate immune cells. B cell activation and survival is dependent on cytokine milieu and TACI activation. TACI is a receptor on B cells that binds to BAFF and APRIL, the TACI fusion will therefore act as inhibitor for BAFF and APRIL. Dual blockade of IgE via upstream pathways will inhibit activation and production of both histamine and allergy causing antibodies limiting the potential for downstream pathway activation.

PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_DESC: LC81686 - ST2 x TL1A Nanobody VHH
ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: Dual targeting of ST2 and TL1A aims to disrupt inflammation and fibrosis at the source. IL-33/ST2 signaling drives inflammation and structural tissue remodeling through pleiotropic actions across diverse immune and non-immune cell types. TL1A drives pro-inflammatory & pro-fibrotic cytokine and growth factor production by multiple cell types. Expected profile of bispecific: Enhanced efficacy by co-blocking epithelial alarmin (IL-33/ST2) and TL1A pathways. Sustained durability through disruption of chronic immune-stromal activation and fibrosis loops. Expanded reach into mixed-type inflammation and fibrostenotic diseases like IBD and chronic lung disease.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach

Dual inhibition of IL-5 and TL1A modulating eosinophilic inflammation and type2, 1/17 & fibrotic pathways, offers comprehensive control of asthma and IBD pathology beyond TNFa and IL-23 therapies. Selective targeting of IL-5 spares key Type2 homeostatic pathways (IL4/IL13), reducing risk of immune deviation and enabling safer long-term intervention.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The TSLP x TACI bispecific aims for combined blockade of TSLP, APRIL and BAFF via a hybrid containing a TACI fusion protein and an anti-TSLP moiety. TACI is a receptor on B cells that binds to BAFF and APRIL, the TACI fusion will therefore act as inhibitor for BAFF and APRIL. The bispecific will control both B-cell-mediated and Type 2 inflammation in asthma and other barrier specific diseases. Elevated TSLP promotes B cell proliferation and activation, which polarize CD4+ naïve T cells into Tfh cells through OX40L. TACI inhibits B cell expansion and promotes the differentiation and survival of plasma cells. Targeting TSLP x TACI effectively controls Type 2 response while also reducing the number of IgE producing cells and downstream IgE-mediated activation of mast cells and basophils.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The OX40 x IgE bispecific aims to raise efficacy ceiling and durability in respiratory diseases by OX40 & IgE dual blockade. OX40 enables pathogenic Th2 cell expansion & memory response to drive chronic allergic inflammation, induces IgE cross-linking  mast cell, basophil and eosinophil activation and degranulation. Enhanced efficacy is expected by breaking the allergic cycle through tackling upstream (OX40-T cell activation) and downstream (IgE-effector) pathways & synergistically lower IgE levels. Combined rapid response & sustained durability can be achieved through dual blockade of IgE-mediated hypersensitivity and pathogenic Teff/mem cells-driven memory responses.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The a4b7 x PD-1 bispecific aims to apply dual brakes on immune cell activation and gut tissue homing via inhibiting both the recruitment & activation of T cells. Both targets are clinically validated with favorable safety profiles. While a4b7 integrin inhibition prevents immune cell recruitment to gut tissue, PD-1 (programmed cell death protein 1) agonism can inhibit immune cell activation & cytokine production.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The a4b7 x IL23p19 bispecific inhibits innate and adaptive immune pathways locally. While a4b7 inhibition prevents immune cell recruitment and activation, IL-23 blockade will suppress ILCs and Th17 within the tissue and restore epithelial barrier function. Both mechanisms are approved in IBD with a favorable safety profile.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The a4b7 x TL1A bispecific aims to break efficacy ceiling in IBD by combining two safe and effective treatments. Both mechanisms are clinically validated in IBD with favorable safety profile. While a4b7 inhibition prevents immune cell recruitment and activation, TL1A inhibition addresses tissue-resident ILCs and fibrosis in addition to dampening pro-inflammatory T cells.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The TSLP x IL5 bispecific aims to raise the efficacy ceiling and address heterogeneity in asthma. TSLP is an upstream initiator for both T cell-mediated type 2 and innate effector-driven non-type 2 inflammation. IL-5 is a driver of collaborative eosinophilic and memory T cell response by enabling eosinophil development and activation. Dual blockade of TSLP-mediated heterogeneous immune response and IL-5-activated eosinophilic inflammation will provide additive benefits to raise efficacy ceiling. Inhibition of IL-5/TSLP-potentiated eosinophilic/memory T cell response will provide an opportunity to extend durable therapeutic response.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: Targeting TL1A and IL7R is expected to promote durable anti-inflammatory, anti-fibrotic & epithelial reparative responses in IBD. IL-7 blockade inhibits T cell pathogenic response regardless of subsets and restores longer-lasting homeostasis through reducing pathogenic Teff/mem cells while preserving Tregs to provide durable efficacy. TL1A amplifies T cell mediated inflammation, fibrosis and barrier dysfunction in barrier tissues by driving pro-inflammatory & pro-fibrotic cytokine and growth factor production by multiple cell types.

PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_DESC: LC81676 - TSLP x AGTR2 Nanobody VHH
ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The TSLP x AGT2R bispecific is expected to resolve chronic lung inflammation and enable improvement in lung function. AGTR2 (angiotensin II type 2 receptor) is a X-linked GPCR receptor, mainly expressed in alveolar type 2 cells. TSLP (thymic stromal lymphopoietin) is a cytokine produced by epithelial cells that activates type 2 immune responses and inflammation by binding to its receptor complex. Activating AGTR2 enables alveolar type 2 cells structure cell regeneration, reduces hypertension as well as inhibits inflammation. A boarder patient population can be reached by targeting to both, the alveolar compartment through AGTR2 and large airways through TSLP, raising the efficacy ceiling in multiple respiratory diseases, such as COPD, asthma, IPF and PAH (co-morbidity).

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The IL1R3 x TL1A bispecific blocks IL1, IL-36, IL-33 and TL1A in one molecule and will allow to double down on inflammation and fibrosis in IBD and beyond. It has high potential to demonstrate increased efficacy as TL1A synergistically boosts pro-inflammatory cytokine production together with IL-1b (ILC activation) or IL-33 (Th9 activation). Furthermore, blocking pro-fibrotic effects of IL-36b will enhance anti-fibrotic properties of aTL1A.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The ST2 x IgE bispecific is designed to interrupt alarmin-driven priming and effector cell activation for synergistic control of type 2 inflammation. IL-33/ST2 signaling drives inflammation and structural tissue remodeling through pleiotropic actions across diverse immune and non-immune cell types. IgE cross-linking induces mast cell activation and degranulation. Expected profile: Enhanced efficacy through dual blockade of upstream (ST2) and downstream (IgE) pathways; prolonged durability by disrupting both immune priming and effector activation loops; broader indication potential beyond classic allergy–targeting mixed and non–IgE-driven type 2 diseases.

PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_DESC: LC81681 - TSLP x C5aR1 Nanobody VHH
ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The TSLP x C5aR1 bispecific aims to control both Type 2 and neutrophilic/innate inflammation to raise efficacy in respiratory disease. TSLP is a key driver of Type 2 allergic and eosinophilic inflammation via DC and ILC2 activation. C5a can aid in Th2 regulation, it also plays a dominant role in neutrophilic inflammation and immune cell recruitment. Synergy with TSLP in immune cell activation and release of proinflammatory mediators is expected. Both, TSLP and C5a can drive collagen production and fibrosis and induce AHR via mast cells. C5a impacts barrier integrity. Targeting the C5a/C5aR1 axis safely controls neutrophilic and innate inflammation while targeting TSLP effectively controls Type 2 response.

PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_DESC: LC81683 - IL6 x OX40L Nanobody VHH
ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The IL6 x OX40L bispecific aims to increase therapy efficacy and durability in AD. OX40L drives Th2 cell expansion and survival, fueling allergic inflammation. It enhances Th2 cytokine production (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13), worsening barrier dysfunction, IgE elevation, and eosinophilic inflammation in AD. IL-6 promotes Th2 and Th17 differentiation, fueling inflammation. It sustains cytokine production via STAT3, drives IgG/IgE production, and impairs skin barrier repair, contributing to AD pathogenesis. Dual IL6 and OX40L inhibition is expected to result in reduced inflammation by lowering STAT3-driven and Th2/Th17 cytokines, an enhanced barrier function via improved keratinocyte differentiation and filaggrin, leading to symptom relief (regarding itch, redness, lichenification).

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The BTLA x OX40 bispecific blocks T cell activation without risk of OX40 cross-linking by potent inhibition of two "checkpoint" pathways with non-immune cell depleting MOAs. Inhibition of both early (BTLA agonism) and late (OX40 antagonism) lymphoid cell activation in the absence of mAb / FcR engagement via localized clustering and blocking of OX40 is expected to result in superior efficacy in diseases as SLE or Atopic dermatitis.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: Dual IL22RA1 x IL-31R blockade promises to broaden patient population and increase efficacy and durability in Atopic Dermatitis. IL22RA1 is upregulated in AD, and mediates IL-22 signaling, promoting epidermal hyperplasia and impairing skin barrier function. Via STAT3 activation, it drives chronic inflammation and reduces barrier proteins like filaggrin, worsening AD symptoms. IL31R, formed by IL31RA and OSMR, mediates IL-31–induced itch by activating sensory neurons and skin cells. Its signaling promotes inflammation, keratinocyte dysfunction, and barrier disruption, worsening AD through increased cytokine production (IL-6, IL-1β, TARC, MCP-1).

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The CD80 x CD28 bispecific aims to induce tolerance and increase efficacy in transplantation and autoimmune diseases via releasing PD-L1 while blocking CD28. A more durable effect is expected versus fusion protein or Fab clinical benchmarks: PD-L1 release induces "natural" agonism of PD-1 by its ligand, while T cell activation is reduced by CD80/CD28 interaction blocking.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The IL23p19 x TL1A bispecific is designed to beat JAK inhibitor efficacy with superior safety. IL-23 is the main regulator of Th17 cells and ILC3s, which may lead to intestinal pathology when dysregulated. aTL1A’s direct anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects will add to the durable efficacy of an IL-23 antagonist. TL1A and IL-23 synergistically drive ILC activation and cytokine production. Both approaches are clinically validated in IBD with excellent safety profile. Targeting these mechanisms will increase efficacy ceiling while keeping safety risk low.

PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_DESC: LC81669 - CD2 x PD1 Nanobody VHH
ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The CD2 x PD1 bispecific aims to achieve PD1 agonism by CD2 anchoring to increase selectivity towards memory T cells and break efficacy ceiling in autoimmune diseases.  Through the proximity of the intracellular tail of PD-1 to a kinase, it induces phosphorylation & downstream signaling. CD2 is also anchoring PD-1 at the immune synapse.  Non-depleting activity compared to benchmarks has the potential for more favorable safety profile. In-vitro, CD2xPD1 bispecifics show better efficacy than benchmarks or their combination. Expected increased selectivity (avidity) towards effector/memory T cells.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: The BTLA x PD1 dual-Agonist is designed to reset T cell immunity and re-establish immune homeostasis in a number of immunological diseases as SLE and RA. It is expected to improve upon PD-1 agonism on immune cells without the potential for long-term safety concerns from T cell depletion while silencing B cell & T cell responses via a combination of immune checkpoint agonism.

PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_DESC: LC81685 - TSLP x OX40L Nanobody VHH
ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Part of the 28 projects on clinically validated targets - bispecific matrix approach
TARGET_RATIONALE: Dual TSLP x OX40L blocking can tackle heterogeneity and chronicity of severe asthma. TSLP is an upstream initiator for both type 2 and non-type 2 inflammation. OX40L/OX40 signals enable pathogenic T cells to drive chronic inflammation beyond IL-4/IL-13 pathway. Dual blockade of TSLP-initiated multiple inflammatory pathways and OX40L-activated heterogeneous T cell response provide opportunity to raise efficacy ceiling. Inhibition of OX40L/TSLP-driven dendritic cell/memory T cell response provides an opportunity to extend durable therapeutic response.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: The current anti-HIV1 trispecific broadly neutralizing antibody  program (LC81120) achieved an M1 on July 8, 2016.  At that time, it was decided that the program would split into two projects:  LC81120 would continue as the trispecific apporach in the clinic.   Additionally, a project code would be created to support the combination of 2 mAb into the clinic.  This request for an LC code will to support the two mAb combination development strategy.
TARGET_RATIONALE: HIV-1 envelope protein gp120/gp41 trimer is the major target for anti-HIV-1 neutralizing activity. It has been demonstrated in various in vitro assays and in vivo animal models that anti-HIV-1 gp120/gp41 neutralizing antibodies can inhibit/prevent HIV-1 infection, reduce/supress viremia, facilitate viral clearance, and diminish the latent viral reservoir. The project  takes advantage of the clinical knowledge surrounding potent and broadly neutralziaing antibodies and combines it with proprietary Sanofi technology in ab formulation and design.    The objectives of the combination of broadly neutralizing antibody project are: 1). Development and optimization of mono-specific anti-HIV-1 neutralizing Abs 2). Identification of lead candidates with best  combination of Abs  3). Preclinical development assesssment: Developability including manufacturability [yield, in vitro stability, solubility, formulation at high concentration(>50 mg/ml)]. In vivo characterization: PD/PK, in vivo stability, potency using NHP(Rhesus macaque) model.

TARGET_RATIONALE: The cystine/glutamate antiporter system xc- transports one molecule of cystine inside the cell in exchange for release of one molecule of glutamate into the extracellular space.  The system xc- is composed of 2 chains linked by a disulfide bridge; a heavy 4F2 chain necessary for membrane localization of the heterodimer, and a light xCT chain responsible for substrate specificity and transport activity.  xCT is constitutively expressed at low levels in the brain and in monocytes and is upregulated by oxidative stress and immune activation, respectively. The system xc- provides the cell with cystine which is reduced to cysteine, the rate-limiting amino acid in the synthesis of the antioxidant glutathione (GSH).  Despite the potential antioxidant benefit of GSH synthesis, evidence suggests that the release of excitatory glutamate in exchange for cystine contributes to neurodegeneration via glutamate-induced cytotoxicity resulting in oligodendrocyte cell death, demyelination and neuronal cell death (Conrad & Sato, 2011, Amino Acids).  Glutamate levels as well as xCT mRNA levels were found to be elevated in the CNS and peripheral blood of MS patients and correlated with disease activity.  Infiltrating monocytes and activated microglial cells in MS and EAE lesions showed high levels of xCT expression and circulating monocytes were shown to produce glutamate upon activation (Pampliega et al, 2011, J Neuroimmunoinflammation).  It has been postulated that while the induction of xCT may play a beneficial role in protection against oxidative stress, the glutamate release by activated monocytes/microglial cells has an overall detrimental effect on neuronal cells and oligodendrocytes.. The biology of xCT supports an approach directed at inhibiting the toxic release of glutamate by activated macrophages/microglial cells in the CNS without impairing their beneficial repair activities.

TARGET_RATIONALE: The objective of this program is to develop a First-in-Class central nervous system TMEM175 agonist to restore lysosomal function and prevent neurodegeneration for treatment of Parkinson’s Disease (PD). TMEM175 has been identified as a common genetic risk factor for PD across multiple genome- wide association studies (GWAS). TMEM175 loss of function (LoF) variants have been associated with increased incidence of PD and decreased age on onset for disease. The most highly prevalent variant, rs34311866 occurs in about 20% of PD patients and has a PD odds ratio of 1.26. Interestingly, gain of function (GoF) variants in TMEM175 have also been identified, spice variants such as rs34884217 reduce disease risk, lowering in the PD odds ratio to 0.75. The identification of TMEM175 variants in PD and Lewy Body Dementia (LBD) support the restoration of lysosomal function via TMEM175 as a viable therapeutic strategy. Lysosomes support proper cellular homeostasis within the cell including proper protein turnover/clearance, phagocytosis, autophagy, and mitochondrial health. Lysosomal dysfunction has been elucidated as a driver of neurodegeneration. Alterations within the lysosome can lead to hydrolase depletion, metabolite building up and pH instability in the lysosome. Improper lysosomal pH drives lysosomal dysregulation resulting in reduced autophagosome clearance and fusion, dysregulated mitophagy and mitochondrial health, and aggregation of alpha-synuclein. TMEM175 is a lysosomal membrane channel which is responsible for maintaining the membrane potential and subsequent lysosomal pH through the conductance of both potassium and protons. Human PD patients display decreased levels of TMEM175 within the brain, particularly in the substantia nigra. Agonism of TMEM175 with a small molecule will reinstate proper proton and potassium efflux across the lysosomal membrane, restoring lysosomal pH and function in neurodegenerative diseases such as PD. 	To develop TMEM175 small molecule agonists we have developed tools to enable a high throughput screening (HTS) approach to identify tool compounds and potential novel small molecules. Primary screening will include florescence-based thallium mobilization and automated electrophysiology assays on recombinant TMEM175 expressing cell lines.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Although patients with mild and moderate asthma usually respond well to glucocorticoids, severe asthma and COPD are generally glucocorticoid-resistant. Various mechanisms that lead to glucocorticoid resistance have been proposed but not well understood.  However, oxidative stress that leads to a defect in HDAC activity is commonly implicated in glucocorticoid resistance. A number of chemically-distinct compounds have been reported to increase steroid responsiveness in vitro. For example, theophylline inhibits LPS-induced reduction of HDAC activity and increases steroid responsiveness of LPS-treated airway macrophages. Curcumin (a polyphenol) restores HDAC activity and increases steroid responsiveness in oxidant-stressed monocytic U937 cells. SH5 (Akt inhibitor), wortmannin (Akt / PI3K inhibitor) and LY-294002 (PI3K inhibitor) restore HDAC activity and increase steroid responsiveness. CpG oligonucleotides have been shown to increase a ?biomarker of steroid responsiveness? in PBMC from steroid-resistant patients. Thus, we propose a phenotypic screening to identify compounds that could restore the glucocorticoid-responsiveness of oxidant-stressed inflammatory cells and could provide a novel therapy for severe asthma and COPD.  #  The target and biochemical pathway need to be de-convoluted after the hits are identified from the phenotypic screening.

TARGET_RATIONALE: The genetic and mechanistic basis of Cystic Fibrosis (CF), a progressive pulmonary disease, is unambiguous. CF is a recessive disease caused by loss-of-function mutations in the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance regulator (CFTR), a cAMP-regulated chloride channel. The most common clinically-important mutation is deletion of phenylalanine at residue 508 (ΔF508-CFTR), within the first Nucleotide Binding domain (NBD1) of the channel. As a consequence, mutant CFTR fails to traffic to the apical membrane and function normally, but instead is retained in the ER and targeted for degradation.. The molecular pathology of the ΔF508-CFTR mutation reflects its two partially independent effects on CFTR.. • ΔF508-CFTR decreases the thermal stability of CFTR’s NBD1  domain, rendering it unstable at physiological temperatures.. • ΔF508-CFTR compromises a key interaction between CFTR’s NBD1 domain and the fourth intracellular loop (ICL4) of CFTR’s second transmembrane domain, impeding CFTR domain-domain assembly.. The goal of the program is to identify small molecule drugs that directly correct the molecular pathology of CF and achieve levels of CFTR function (specified in section 4) that, singly or in combination, would substantially reduce the burden of CF in the vast majority of patients.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Identification of antibody-drug conjugates targeting carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), using antibody "15B4" as a starting point.M2 planned: April 17, 2013
TARGET_RATIONALE: CEA was first described in 1965 as a gastrointestinal oncofetal antigen. CEA belongs to the CEACAM family and is a GPI anchored membrane protein.  CEA is involved in tumor cell adhesion, invasion, metastasis and is proposed to display anti-apoptotic effect. Its function and role in cancer is still unclear.. An anti-CEA antibody, 15B4, was identified by East Carolina University during the collaboration with IMGN, and this antibody was used to validate a number of criteria, including CEA expression in normal tissues and tumor tissues, internalization, cellular activity. Based on the results obtained, CEA was qualified as a good target for ADC and 15B4 was identified as a good starting point to develop this ADC.. Due to its high prevalence and high density of expression in colon tumors, CEA appears a particularly suitable target for a treatment with an ADC in this indication. We propose to investigate 15B4 conjugation to our new tomaymycin cytotoxic molecule. Indeed CRC are not sensitive to tubulin binders but respond to DNA binding agents. This makes tomaymycin a very good candidate for the development of an ADC in CRC. In addition, as of today, we have no ADC targeting CRC.. The first goal of the project would thus be to develop an anti-CEA(15B4)-linker-Tomaymycin for the treatment of CRC.. CEA being also expressed in a number of tumors potentially sensitive to tubulin agents (like lung tumors), we also would like to evaluate the potential value of an anti-CEA(15B4) coupled to Cryptophycin or Maytansin.. During this project we would like to explore 2 axes: as a priority 1, explore cysteine conjugation in parallel to the standard lysine conjugation (this requires the production of cysteine engineered antibodies in parallel to the "wt" mAb; as a priority 2,  we would like to explore the added value of bispecific anti-CEA antibodies composed of 15B4 and a second anti CEA targeting a different epitope.

Harnessing Warp Drive Bio (WDB) proprietary technology, the project aims at discovering novel AGs overcoming the main mechanisms of resistance and displaying good activities vs pseudomonas while presenting a better safety profile than historical AGs. The corresponding biosynthetic gene clusters will be then transferred to heterologous strains to cleanly produce extracts containing the expected new NPs. . Following microbiological testing against a panel of relevant Gram(-), the active extracts will be then dereplicated and the active components isolated for structure elucidation and confirmation of activity. Hit compound(s) fulfilling the targeted antibacterial profile will be optimized at Sanofi by semi-synthesis toward a lead and then a clinical candidate.

TNFAIP6 (TSG-6), a 35 kDa secreted protein and member of the hyaluronan-binding protein family, is expressed in response to inflammatory mediators and growth factors, and acts as a joint protective modulator through several pathways. TSG6 e.g. induces a dramatic increase in the anti-plasmin activity of Inter-a-inhibitor (IaI), and thus excerts a chondroprotective effect through inactivation of the metalloprotease network. Furthermore, TSG6 inhibits RANKL-induced osteoclast activation and differentiation from precursor cells. TSG6 has anti-inflammatory and osteo-/chondro-protective properties, making it an endogenous inhibitor of joint destruction and osteoporosis (Milner et al., 2006). Studies with recombinant TSG6 (full length as well as truncated, and mutants thereof) for the treatment of arthritis and for inhibition of bone resorption have been published (e.g. Bardos et al., 2001; Mindrescu et al., 2002; Mahoney et al., 2008). Cartilage damage, as well as aggrecanase and metalloproteinase activity are significantly reduced in mouse models (AIA, CIA, PGIA) overexpressing cartilage-specific TSG6, or after injection of recombinant TSG6. In contrast, TSG6-/- mice get e.g. accelerated and more severe PGIA with more extensive cartilage damage than wild-type controls (Mindrescu et al., 2002; Glant et al., 2002; Mahoney et al., 2008).

HVEM (Herpes virus entry mediator or TNFRSF14) is a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor family. HVEM is a TNF receptor family member with four natural ligands that either stimulate (LIGHT, LTbeta) or inhibit (BTLA, CD160) T cell function. This protein plays a central role in the development of the immune system and may function as a costimulatory factor for the activation of lymphoid cells and as a deterrent to infection by herpes virus. This protein has been shown to stimulate the proliferation of T cells, and trigger apoptosis of various tumor cells. This protein is also reported to prevent tumor necrosis factor alpha mediated apoptosis in primary hepatocyte. A region in the CRD1 domain of some TNFR-like receptors can self-associate = PLAD (Pre-Ligand Assembly Domain). This allows the assembly (di- or tri-merization) of the receptors in the absence of ligand, through a distinct domain from the ligand binding site, and thus promotes receptor function. Despite structural similarities, strong differences in amino acid sequences of CRD1 for TNFR-like receptors. Deletion or blockade of HVEM CRD1 abolishes the binding of CD160 and BTLA, but not LIGHT, and converts HVEM to a dominant costimulatory molecule. The purpose is to select small selective molecules capable of inhibiting the pre-oligomerization of the receptor HVEM (through interaction with the PLAD domain) and therefore block the signaling and cell responses induced by this receptor.

The aim of this project is the synthesis of pseudo-oligosaccharides that mimic biologically relevant molecules. Monosaccharide units will be synthesized, bearing a suitable alkyl chain with a terminal double-bond. An intermolecular cross-methatesis (CM) reaction carried out with Hoveyda or Grubbs catalyst will allow the formation of a new C-C double bond between the two different units. An intramolecular cyclization promoted by electrophilic activation of the newly formed C-C double bond will then afford a tricyclic compound that mimics a trisaccharide. The obtained fragments will be used to coat gold nanoparticles (GNPs).Gold nanoparticles are water soluble, stable in solution for years and non cytotoxic. Their synthesis is consolidated and allows to obtain particles with reduced dispersion and controlled size. A carbohydrate functionalized GNP is reported to be an appropriate multivalent system to mimic the multivalent presentation of ligands at active site, a common feature in natural carbohydrate-mediated interactions. GNPs represent a nice alternative to other carrier, behaving as an handy support to obtain versatile tools. The obtained nanoparticles can be easily functionalized with a variety of suitably thiolated ligands. The possibility to obtain a "hybrid" monolayer composition is well known, allowing to widen the application field.

TNFRI (TNF-receptor 1 or CD120a) is a 55 kD transmembrane glycoprotein that also exists as a secreted protein. It is widely expressed and is present on the cell surface as a trimer of 55 kDa subunits. It serves as a receptor for both TNFα and TNFβ/lymphotoxin. This receptor can activate NF-kappaB, mediate apoptosis, and function as a regulator of inflammation. A region in the CRD1 domain of some TNFR-like receptors can self-associate = PLAD (Pre-Ligand Assembly Domain). This allows the assembly (di- or trimerization) of the receptors in the absence of ligand, through a distinct domain from the ligand binding site, and thus promotes receptor function. Despite structural similarities, strong differences in amino acid sequences of CRD1 for TNFR-like receptors. PLAD peptide derived from TNFR-1 potently inhibits TNF-induced cell death and NF-KB activation, and was highly effective against arthritis induced by intra-articular injection of TNF and collagen-induced arthritis.The purpose is to select small selective molecules capable of inhibiting the pre-oligomerization of the receptor TNFR1 (through interaction with the PLAD domain) and therefore block the signaling and cell responses induced by this receptor.

MG53 mediates insulin resistance via IR & IRS1 degradation, thus is a potential therapeutic target for development of anti-diabetic drugs.. Literature example: Yi et al., Nature Communications Volume: 4, Article number:2354 - MG53-induced IRS-1 ubiquitination negatively regulates skeletal myogenesis and insulin signaling. Mitsugumin 53 (MG53) negatively regulates skeletal myogenesis by targeting insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS-1). Here, we show that MG53 is an ubiquitin E3 ligase that induces IRS-1 ubiquitination with the help of an E2-conjugating enzyme, UBE2H. Molecular manipulations that disrupt the E3-ligase function of MG53 abolish IRS-1 ubiquitination and enhance skeletal myogenesis. Skeletal muscles derived from the MG53-/- mice show an elevated IRS-1 level with enhanced insulin signaling, which protects the MG53-/- mice from developing insulin resistance when challenged with a high-fat/high-sucrose diet. Muscle samples derived from human diabetic patients and mice with insulin resistance show normal expression of MG53, indicating that altered MG53 expression does not serve as a causative factor for the development of metabolic disorders. Thus, therapeutic interventions that target the interaction between MG53 and IRS-1 may be a novel approach for the treatment of metabolic diseases that are associated with insulin resistance

TARGET_RATIONALE: Huntington's Disease (HD) is a fatal, progressively degenerative brain disorder for which only symptomatic treatments but no efficacious anti-neurodegenerative therapy exists at present.  The disease is caused by an expansion of glutamine repeats (polyQ, >35 glutamine residues) at the N-terminal part of a large protein called huntingtin (HTT), which is ubiquitously expressed. Death occurs within 15-20 years of disease onset and onset is inversely correlated to the number of CAG repeats.  With the identification of the underlying genetic basis of HD, therapies are being developed that reduce expression of the causative mutant HTT protein.  Strategies which selectively reduce the expression of mutant HTT have shown therapeutic benefits in animal models of the disease. Genzyme has an active interest in HTT lowering strategies and recently partnered our AAV-RNAi program with Voyager Therapeutics.  /  We are interested in enriching the project pipeline activities to include small molecules that may achieve HTT protein lowering without the complications of AAV gene therapy delivery or miRNA off target liabilities.  Evotec has substantial expertise in industrial HD R&D.  They have a well-established integrated drug discovery platform capable of carrying projects from assay development, screen, to H2L and beyond.   The goal of this project is to progress from HTS to high quality lead to candidate status in 4 years (Pre-DC transition).  This project will leverage the 2 Master Service Agreements in place with Evotec (France/Toulouse and Germany/Hamburg) as well as leverage Evotec exclusive capabilities, expertise and relationship with CHDI Foundation.

TARGET_RATIONALE: new: Autoimmune diseases and chronic inflammatory conditions such as e.g. psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease, and rheumatoid arthritis have been defined as clinical syndromes that result from inappropriate activation of T cells, B cells, or both, and in which autoimmunity demonstrated by selfreactive T cells or antibodies play a causative or a significant contributory role. Effector CD4+ T cells are subdivided into different subsets. Th2 cells, which produce the marker cytokines IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13, are mainly involved in allergic and helminth responses, whereas Th1 cells, on the other hand, contribute to the elimination of intracellular pathogens and are involved in cell-mediated and delayed-type hypersensitivity responses. Th17 cells like Th1 cells, have the capacity to cause T-cell-mediated inflammation and autoimmune disease. The heterogeneity among immune cells is determined by multiple growth factors, cytokines, and other extracellular modulators of multiple signaling pathways, and there exists a high degree of plasticity within the system. The overall goal for this project is the identification and validation of new targets that are based on the modulation of aberrant immune cell regulation with focus on Th1/Th17 driven autoimmunity in order to treat diseases such as e.g. different forms of arthritis, psoriasis, or IBD.   #  old: The prevalence of chronic diseases is on the rise and includes common conditions such as heart disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and chronic inflammatory conditions such as e.g. psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease, and arthritis. Inflammation plays a role in the pathogenesis of almost all chronic diseases, and common inflammation pathways underlie numerous diseases regardless of the tissue affected. Furthermore, inflammation in one organ can have systemic effects and disrupt distant physiologic sites. Inflammation is also an important aspect of healing, playing a key role in resolving disease and promoting restitution of injured tissues. Inflammation therefore is an important therapeutic target for many common chronic diseases that affect a large portion of the population. The overall objective is to develop new anti-inflammatory drugs that can be used to treat humans with chronic inflammatory diseases.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Evotec Project  #  Identification of compounds, which reverse the Warburg effect.Indication: agressive tumors
TARGET_RATIONALE: In contrast to normal differentiated cells, which rely primarily on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) to generate the energy needed for cellular processes, most cancer cells instead, and particularly those described to have an "aggressive pattern", rely on aerobic glycolysis, a phenomenon termed "the Warburg effect". This shift from OXPHOS to glycolysis leads for metabolism to be independent from mitochondrial involvement. Since mitochondria are one major actor in the regulation of cell death, this adaptation contributes to the resistance of aggressive cancer cells to chemotherapy. The goal of our phenotypic approach is to shift back (reverse the Warburg effect) tumor cell metabolism from glycolysis to OXPHOS with small molecules. In that context, we have already developed an assay that allows the determination of the balance between OXPHOS and glycolysis in tumor cells and we have chosen a cancer cell line that presents a purely glycolytic pattern (MDA-MB). The assay is easy to use and consists in measuring ATP production from glycolysis and OXPHOS (luciferase read out on cell lysates) and is ready to transfer to LGCR for a phenotypic screen. In parallel, we have already developed numerous secondary and functional assays to support deorphaning of the compounds in E2C.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Tumor necrosis factor alpha blockade, achieved by the use of soluble receptors (Etanercept/Enbrel approved in 1998) or anti TNF-alpha antibodies (infliximab/cA2/Remicade approved in 1999, Adalimumab/D2E7/Humira approved in 2002), has been a major success in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. This success has highlighted the key role of inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in the development of rheumatoid arthritis, but also of Crohn's disease, psoriasis and COPD where these inflammatory mediators are also involved. Infliximab is also licensed for Crohn's disease and anti-TNF-alpha biological agents have shown major promise in spondyloarthropathies, psoriasic arthritis and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. However, there are problems with these anti-TNF-alpha biological agents, that limit their use. From a safety perspective, although TNF-alpha blockade has not demonstrated susceptibility to infections, some patients experienced tuberculosis, and problems of antigenicity, linked to the use of proteins, require the concomitant use of immunosuppressive drugs, i.e. methotrexate. Moreover, the difficulty in producing proteins on a mass scale is a problem, specially for Etanercept/Enbrel. However, by far, the biggest constraint is the cost of treatment, which is of the order of $15000/patient/year. This has led to a low uptake of these treatments in several European countries and is considered as  economic failures in the USA.The main hope is to find ways of blocking TNF-alpha production or functions with small molecular weight inhibitors that are orally bioavailable and cheaper. However, only few molecules have already reached clinical development phases. Considering the possibility  that these existing small molecular weight inhibitors are less active than the approved biological blockers, we have screened for orally active agents that are very potent to concomitantly inhibit the synthesis of TNF-alpha, but also of the chemokine MCP-1, which is highly involved in the migration of inflammatory cells toward the lesions of rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis and of many autoimmune diseases.

NOTES..#/# Despite significant efforts in therapeutics and diagnostics over the past decades, viable treatments and diagnostic tools for synulceinopathies are still lacking. Proper detection and diagnosis are crucial for guiding treatment options and effectively managing patients an early stage. Recently, two radioligands for PET imaging of abnormally folded alpha-syn have been studied in humans by AC Immune and QST/JP. However, their accessibility is limited to MAS only, leaving no PET tracers available for PD and DLB.
TARGET_RATIONALE: The aim of this project is to develop new PET tracers that can accurately and non-invasively quantify misfolded alpha-synuclein (alpha-syn) inclusion bodies in the brain, which are a key pathological feature of Parkinson’s disease (PD), Dementia with Lewy Body (DLB), and Multiple System Atrophy (MSA). The current diagnosis of these autonomic synucleinopathies relies on clinical tests with inadequate biomarkers and analytical tools, highlighting the critical unmet need for effective disease management. Although small compound-based radioligands have been investigated, their poor specificity and stability have limited their effectiveness, particularly in brain PET imaging. To address this challenge, antibodies have been developed for immuno-PET. Specifically, by combining anti-alpha-syn with brain shuttle molecules (anti-TfR or anti-IGF1R), novel bispecific fusion molecules will be created and evaluated. This alpha-syn immuno-PET will allow for direct measurement of pathological alpha-syn levels and their spatiotemporal distribution in the brain. It will provide diagnostic and prognostic markers for patient’s identification and stratification, as well as for monitoring therapeutic efficacies and facilitating drug development efforts. This project will support internal clinical trial (SAR446159/ABL301) and therapeutic development (gene therapy, AAV-GG2) and may lead to commercialization with an external partnership.

TARGET_RATIONALE: The Discoidin Domain Receptor 1 (DDR1) is a receptor tyrosine kinase that is activated by type I to VI and VIII collagen, shown to be involved in the regulation of cell adhesion, migration, proliferation, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling and differentiation of multiple cell types. Emerging evidence suggest important roles for DDR1 in the pathogenesis of various human diseases, in particular during tumor progression, renal damage, tissue fibrosis, atherosclerosis and inflammation:1) DDR1 has been linked to a number of diverse human cancers via studies on tumor cell lines or clinical tumor samples. DDR1 was shown to be more highly expressed in cancerous breast epithelial cells relative to normal breast epithelial tissue. Furthermore, DDR1 has been demonstrated to be a direct transcriptional target of the p53 tumor suppressor gene, highlighting a possible role in carcinogenesis per se. Inhibition of DDR1 in cells containing wild type p53 results in increased apoptosis, suggesting DDR1 as a potential target in cancer therapy. 2) DDR1 is up-regulated 2 fold in tubulo-interstitial biopsies from patients with diabetic nephropathy (DN), and its up-regulation correlates with the severity of the disease. Furthermore, DDR1 is up-regulated in glomeruli of a renal injury rat model as well as in glomeruli and in renal vessels of Ang II-treated mice with hypertension. DDR1 KO mice are protected against hypertension-induced renal disease. In contrast to wild type mice, DDR1 KO mice show in the hypertension-induced renal failure model (AngII-induced hypertension) a marked reduction in sclerotic glomeruli, proteinuria, leukocyte infiltration and in collagen I and IV deposition. In addition, DDR1 suppression in vivo (siRNA mediated) attenuates markedly the development of bleomycin-induced pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis.3) DDR1 may play important roles in the progression of atherosclerosis. Its deletion decreases atherosclerosis by accelerating matrix accumulation and reducing inflammation in low-density lipoprotein receptor-deficient mice.These data support the concept of DDR1as being a molecular sensor that can probe the integrity of the extracellular matrix in a wide variety of conditions. With this notion in mind, DDR1 shall be well positioned to qualify as cell-surface accessible target for potential therapeutic interventions.

ARAF, BRAF and CRAF (HUGO symbol: RAF1) are a family of three protein-serine/threonine kinases that participate in the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signal transduction cascade. RAS-GTP leads to the activation of RAF kinase which in turn phosphorylates and activates MEK1/2. MEK1/2, then, activates ERK1/2 which is involved in regulating cell survival, proliferation, senescence, and differentiationRAS is the oncogene most frequently mutated in human cancer with ~ 33% of all tumors expressing activated RAS. Most cancers with somatic RAS mutations harbor changes in KRAS (85% including pancreas, lung and colon), whereas NRAS mutations are less common (15% including melanoma, liver and myeloid cancers) and HRAS mutations are rare (< 1% usually urogenital tumors). Despite extensive efforts, targeted therapies against RAS were largely unsuccessful and thus the inhibition of RAS effector pathways may represent a more feasible approach to eradicate RAS mutant cancers. Recently, several studies demonstrated in lung cancer mouse models that cRAF and not BRAF is essential in for tumor initiation by oncogenic KRAS suggesting that selective CRAF inhibitors could be of interest to tackle tumors harboring a RAS mutation.Potential indication: tumors harboring a KRAS mutation (including lung, pancreas, colon)

TARGET_RATIONALE: (I) T2Diabetes: Increased plasma levels of branched-chain amino acids have been linked to development of diabetes. Two different genetic murine models of diminished Scl6a19 activity, the major transporter of branched chain amino acids have improved insulin sensitivity. - (II) Rare Diseases - UCD: Waste nitrogen is carried by glutamine from peripheral tissues to the liver, where it is converted to urea for excretion. Urea cycle disorders (UCD) are caused by inborn deficiencies in one of the enzymes responsible for urea production, leading to toxic levels of systemic ammonia. By reducing dietary uptake and renal recovery of neutral amino acids such as glutamine, SLC6A19 blocker therapy will limit buildup of waste nitrogen in patients with UCD.  - (III) Rare Diseseas: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is caused by a deficiency in the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase, which converts phenylalanine (Phe) to tyrosine, the first step in the primary pathway of Phe catabolism. We hypothesize that preventing the reabsorption of Phe may provide a disposal pathway for Phe via excretion into the urine, and thus theoretically lower systemic Phe levels. We have validated SLC6A19 as a target, demonstrating that lack of SLC6A19 or inhibition of SLC6A19 can promote excretion of Phe in the urine sufficient to significantly lower blood and brain Phe levels in a mouse model of PKU. Pueraria lobata common name Kudzu was imported into the US via Japan in the late 1800s where it is now considered an invasive species.  Extracts of Pueraria are commonly used herbal supplements specifically to promote liver health.  Pueraria has GRAS (generally regarded as safe) status and reported to have a average LD50 of 2-5g/kg in mice.  No known side effects associated with oral Kudzu intake have been reported.  The main bioactive ingredient appears to be puerarin and a group of saponins with literature demonstrated anti-fibrotic activity in in vivo models of hepatotoxicity (CCL4 / Bile Duct Ligation).  Efficacy of Kudzu extracts has been demonstrated in both therapeutic and prophylactic models using two rodent species (mice and rats).  .  Safety profile of Genestein should be carefully studied as the reported potential addictive nature of Puerain extracts should be investigated (CNS exposure) and the need for abuse liability tests considered.  Finally there is a need to look closely at clinical trial information and consider dosing frequency of puerain/ pueria extracts and potential limitations.  The decision by the TSU Fibrosis Botanical Working Group was to accept this botanical for a liver fibrosis indication.

LGR5 is a GPCR belonging to the LGR subfamily (Leucine-rich repeat-containing GPCRs) and very recently RSPO has been proposed as ligand. LGR5 has been identified as a Wnt/beta-catenin target gene in house using a E-cadherin dominant-negative screen and in the literature by many authors (Yamamoto  #  Et al 2006; Barker et al 2007).  Association between beta-catenin activating mutations and LGR5 over expression in cancer patients has been reported (Bioulac-Sage 2007; Zucman-Rossi et al 2007). Up regulation at mRNA and protein level has been described in colorectal and ovarian tumors. Targeted deletion of LGR5 gene in mice (null mice) results in neonatal lethality, 24h after birth (Morita 2004).  Its function in adult tissues is unknown but it is well known as a marker of cancer stem cells on colon & small intestine, Stomach and Mammary gland (Clevers 2008; Barker, 2009). ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Identify and characterize compounds that selectively and positively modulate the allosteric site of the alpha7 nicotinic receptor.former Leading Department: CNS
TARGET_RATIONALE: The target is the allosteric site of the alpha7 nicotinic receptor. In the context of ligand gated ion channels such as nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs), endogenous ligand acetylcholine binds at the orthosteric site and molecules that bind elsewhere on the nAChR subunit(s) acts via allosteric interactions. For example, studies with the homomeric alpha7 nAChRs indicate that such ligand interactions can be well described by an allosteric model, and that positive allosteric effectors can affect energy transitions by (i) predominantly affecting the peak current response (Type I profile) or, (ii) both peak current responses and time course of agonist-evoked response (Type II profile). The recent discovery of a chemically heterogeneous group of molecules capable of differentially modifying nAChR properties without interacting at the ligand binding site illustrates the adequacy of the allosteric model to predict functional consequences.  Selective positive allosteric modulation of nAChRs can be considered as a viable therapeutic approach for these disease states. A key advantage of the PAM approach is that modulation is only revealed in the presence of an endogenous agonist, thereby preserving the temporal and spatial integrity of neurotransmission.

TARGET_RATIONALE: X-linked Adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) is a metabolic neurodegenerative disease caused by mutations in ABCD1 gene encoding the peroxisomal ABC transporter - Adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ALDP) - responsible for the transport of very long chains of fatty acids (VLCFA) to the peroxisome for degradation by beta-oxidation.  Mutations in ABCD1 result in an accumulation of VLCFA (mainly C26:0) in all tissues, especially in the brain and adrenal gland; and this accumulation is thought to be associated with the disease pathology. ELOVL1 (Elongation of very long chain fatty acid protein 1) was identified as the single elongase catalyzing the synthesis of both saturated VLCFA (C26:0) and mono-unsaturated VLCFA (C26:1) and is a limiting factor in this process. We have confirmed that reduction of the ELOVL1 level by siRNA in CCALD patients’ fibroblasts decreases the level of VLCFA (26:0). We propose that a small molecule CNS penetrant inhibitor of ELOVL1 has the potential to normalize VLCFA levels and to prevent disease pathology in patients with X-ALD.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Medicinal uses of Astralagus membranaceus extracts
TARGET_RATIONALE: Astragalus (Astragalus membranaceus) is a flowering perennial plant belonging to the legume family (Fabaceae) native to northern and eastern parts of China as well as Korea and Mongolia.  The plant, specifically the root, has been used in Traditional Chinese Medicine for thousands of years, often in combination with other herbs, to strengthen the body against disease. Astragalus is used as an adaptogen, meaning it helps protect the body against various stresses. It also contains antioxidants, which protect cells against damage caused by free radicals, byproducts of cellular energy.  It is anticipated that initially in vitro assays measuring the degree of protection [cell viability/senescence readouts] afforded small airway epithelial cells from bleomycin or TGF-b induced damage will be used to evaluate Astragalus extract potency. . The unique pharmacology of astragalus extracts appear to be due to its concentration of astragalosides, which are triterpene saponins unique to astragalus.  Astragalosides are telomerase activators, meaning that they activate the telomerase enzyme and increase telomere length.  Telomeres are the protective ends on chromosomes, and increased telomerase function has been shown to promote cellular longevity under conditions of stress by blocking chromosomal degradation.  . Astragalus has a history of human use for kidney and liver fibrosis.  Astragalus also has antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties and is sometimes used topically for wounds.  Finally, Astragalus extracts are of high interest for testing in models of lung fibrosis, because idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in humans has been linked to mutations that cause decreased telomerase activity.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Objective:  Identification of compounds that inhibit the signalling pathways leading to translocation of class II HDACs from the nucleus into the cytoplasm.
TARGET_RATIONALE: Class II HDACs have been described as having a key role in cardiac hypertrophy by switching on the so-called fetal gene program. In response to neurohumoral stimulation, PKD and CaMKII become activated and phosphorylate HDAC that is bound to the transcription factor MEF2 and suppresses its activity. The phosphorylated sites on HDAC are recognised by the 14-3-3 protein, and binding of 14-3-3 leads to dissociation of HDAC from MEF2 and its export from the nucleus into the cytoplasm.  Thus, HATs can bind to and activate MEF2, thereby leading to the transcription of genes involved in abnormal cardiac growth. The idea of the phenotypic approach is not to interfere with the catalytic activity of HDAC (logically we would go for activators but, paradoxically, HDAC inhibitors (probably of the class I enzymes) have been shown to be beneficial in suppressing cardiac hypertrophy), but with the cellular signalling that leads to dissociation from MEF2 and nuclear export.

So, reducing KYNA levels by inhibiting the KAT-II synthesis enzyme would enhance the NMDA-mediated glutamatergic and alpha7-mediated cholinergic tones, and might have potential therapeutic activity in schizophrenia, in bipolar mania and others diseases associated with cognitive/memory impairments (Alzheimer).

TARGET_RATIONALE: CX3CR1 is a G-protein-coupled seven-transmembrane chemokine receptor expressed on monocytes, macrophages, NK/T cell subsets, and dendritic cells. CX3CR1 activation leads to a) rapid capture/adhesion, b) chemotaxis, c) retention and d) pro-survival signaling in immune cells.  CX3CL1 is a well-established ligand for CX3CR1. CX3CL1 is a membrane-bound chemokine possessing a chemokine/mucin hybrid structure and a transmembrane domain and has a dual function as an adhesion molecule and a chemoattractant. CX3CL1 acts as an adhesion molecule in the membrane-bound form or as a chemoattractant in the soluble form shed by metalloproteases, ADAM10/17. Human genetics data and preclinical evidence suggest a key role for CX3CR1 in SLE, RA and IBD pathogenesis. Importantly, CX3CL1-CX3CR1 is a clinically validated pathway in Rheumatoid Arthritis, anti-CX3CL1 antibodies showed some degree of efficacy in Phase II for RA. Anti-CX3CR1 nanobody developed at Boehringer Ingelheim in the context of a collaboration with Ablynx demonstrated significant reduction in the incidence of glomerular lesions and glomerulosclerosis in human CX3CR1 knock-in mice and have shown a high safety and tolerability profile in Phase I studies.  #/#  Objective of this program is the further optimization and development of anti-CX3CR1 Nb molecules from the Ablynx/BI collaboration as therapeutics in Lupus Nephritis, Rheumatoid ARthritis, Asthma, Atopic Dermatitis.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Ciliopathies are a class of genetic disorders that result from mutations in genes that disrupt the formation or function of the primary cilium, a key cellular signaling center found in most cells. Gangliosides are a class of membrane lipid that is an important component of membrane microdomains responsible for cellular signaling activity, including lipid rafts and primary cilia; GM3 synthase (GM3S, the product of the ST3GAL5 gene) catalyzes the first step of ganglioside formation. Evidence suggests that blocking GM3 accumulation slows disease progression in several mouse models of different ciliopathies, including models of both Polycystic Kidney Disease and Bardet-Biedl Syndrome. Further, our data suggests that the mechanism of action involves restoration of primary cilia structure and signaling activity. Therefore, GM3S inhibition provides an attractive approach to treat ciliopathies by restoring the dysregulated signaling activity that drives disease progression.

TARGET_RATIONALE: The objective is to generate inhibitors of Histone Lysine Methyl Transferase (SET domain protein). Methylation of Histone is one of the post-translational modification affecting gene expression. Methylation occur at Arginine or lysine of the H3 and H4 Histone tail. Several histone methyl transferase (HMT) have been discovered and fall into two categories according to their ability to methylate lysine or arginine residues. Lysine-specific HMTs contain a conserved motif named SET domain and have been classified into four groups according to homology within the SET domain. The targeted HLMT are : SUV39H1; SMYD3; EZH2. Double knockout mice Suv39h1/2 have a predisposition to cancer with non segregated chromosomes. Recently it was show that SUV39H1 and Rb interact in vivo and that both protein are required for regulation of the gene encoding cyclinE regulator of the G1 to S phase transition. There have been several SET domain genes that have been implicated in cancer (Schneider)]. Most recently, the EZH2 polycomb group protein HMT has been shown to be overexpressed in metastatic prostate cancer and breast and the SET domain of MLL are frequently found implicated  in human leukaemias. The oncogenic potential of this protein is also demonstrated by siRNA against EZH2 inhibiting prostate cell proliferation.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is a multi-systemic spliceopathy caused by CTG repeats expansion at the 3'UTR of DMPK gene. The mRNA carrying >50 CUG repeats aggregates with RNA binding proteins, which leads to a dysregulation of alternative splicing. Since DM1 is caused by the gain-of-toxic-function of  the mutated DMPK mRNA, removal of DMPK mRNA is the most direct target for this indication. DMPK mRNA reduction has been validated in-house using antisense oligonucleotides with a collaboration with Ionis and external Phase1/2 clinical trials using the ASO approach are ongoing by Ionis/Biogen. DMPK mRNA degradation appeared to be safe in their phase I clinical trial. The aim of this project is to deliver a short nucleotide that induce DMPK mRNA silencing to muscle by using Adeno-associated virus. In parallel with generating the preclinical PoC data using AAV9 as a vehicle, a new capsid with a narrow tropism to muscles and a capability to evade from human IVIg will be generated/selected.

PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_DESC: LC80453 - iPS-based Cardiac Precursor Cell Differentiation
ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Generation of cardiac precursor cells from induced pluripotent stem cells and their differentiation into cardiomyocytes by small molecules.
TARGET_RATIONALE: Adult heart contains a limited number of cardiac progenitor cells (CPC). Activation of proliferation and differentiation of these cells could be beneficial for the treatment of myocardial infarction (MI) and heart failure independently from a cause. Isolation of these cells from the adult, especially human heart is not feasible. Therefore we plan to develop a model based on the differentiation of human induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs) into CPC. Primary human fibroblasts (or other primary cells of human origin) will be transduced with several lentiviral constructs to overexpress transcription factors necessary for the dedifferentiation into pluripotent cells (Oct4, Klf4, Sox2, Nanog, c-Myc). These iPSCs will be used to introduce genetic reporter systems containing early and late heart-specific promoters controlling two different fluorescent proteins, eg GFP and RFP. CPC will be isolated based on the activity of the early promoter (Nkx2-5-GFP) either as a result of spontaneous differentiation of the iPSCs or directed differentiation through forced expression of the heart-specific early transcription factors, like Nkx2-5 and Hand1. Obtained CPCs will be used for phenotypical screening with a compound library to identify small molecules causing proliferation and differentiation of these cells into cardiomyocytes. Activation of the late cardio-specific reporter, eg alphaMHC (Myosin Heavy Chain, alpha) controlling an additional fluorescent protein, eg RFP, will serve as a readout. As a side product of this assay development we expect the generation of typical human cardiomyocytes which can be used for a number of other applications within the Cardiovascular TD. The pluripotent  nature of the iPSCs will allow their use outside CV TD, as well.  #  Necessary lentiviral constructs will be either generated internally or licensed.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Prostaglandins, including PGE2 are produced in substantial amounts during allergen exposure and disease development. Prostaglandin E2 acts at four specific cell surface receptors (EP1 - EP4) to elicit its own actions. Of the four EP receptors, the EP3 and EP4 bind Prostaglandin E2 with the highest affinity. The PGE2-EP3 pathway is an important negative modulator of allergic reaction. The mechanism of action of an EP3 agonist comprises the inhibition of antigen-induced infiltration of inflammatory cells, the supression of allergen-induced mediator release like histamin and the inhibition of allergy-related gene expression (genes encoding  chemokines, Clca3, Muc5ac, MMP-12, ADAM-8 and Alox15). Therefore, the EP3 receptor represents a target of great interest for finding new antiallergy drugs.

TARGET_RATIONALE: IL-4 and IL-13 are dominant cytokines in Type 2 biology, driving many allergic diseases, and utilize JAK1 and STAT6 for activation and signalling. The IL-4/IL-13 pathway has been clinically credentialed in several Type 2 diseases e.g. Atopic Dermatitis, Asthma and Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps. The objective of the project is to develop an oral STAT6-selective degrader using a PROTAC (CTM) modality in collaboration with Nurix. This would potentialy have similar  efficacy to Dupixent, but with more selectivity than JAK inhibitors, for therapeutic use in Type 2/TH2-mediated inflammatory disease.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Medicinal uses of Panax ginseng / notoginseng extracts
TARGET_RATIONALE: Ginseng is a well-known herbal medicine from Asia.   The genus Panax contains eleven distinct species of slow-growing perennial plants with fleshy roots, growing typically in cooler climates with a widespread distribution in the Northern Hemisphere.  Only two major species have traditionally been used in China: Panax ginseng (native Northeast China) and Panax notoginseng (native Southwest China).  Ginseng preparations have been used traditionally for medicinal purposes (as adaptogens [anti-stress], nourishing stimulants, type II diabetes, sexual dysfunction, wound healing), in foods and drinks and in cosmetic preparations. Despite widespread use ginseng has not been commercialized for wound healing. . The principal active constituents of the Panax plants are saponins (triterpene glycosides). Collectively this class of active Panax compounds are known as Ginsenosides.  Because of ginseng's widespread use this class has been well characterized with ~ 25 identified.  Ginseng species have different proportions of these components as well as different percentages of them.    Ginseng extracts and isolated components have been reported in the literature to be efficacious in several chronic and acute wound healing models (diabetic, burn wounds, scarring).  Extracts are shown to modulate multiple mechanisms of relevance including angiogenesis, increasing collagen synthesis, Pro-tPA, anti-TGF, decreased alpha-SMA and hemeostasis.  . Ginseng extracts have a long history of safe use, supported by both chronic exposure animal and human clinical studies. Ginseng is approved as a food additive in the US, sold OTC in the EU and is Commission E (Germany) approved.  Although ginseng extraction/purification protocols are well characterized, significant developmental opportunity is thought to exist around a topically applied combination product, for example a broad class similarity between bioactive ginseng and centella triterpenes may result in a combination product with overlapping properties possibly resulting in enhanced treatment efficacy.

TARGET_RATIONALE: An expanded hexanucleotide (G4C2) in C9ORF72 is the leading genetic cause of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) in Europe and North America.  The G4C2 repeat expansion triggers three non-mutually exclusive disease pathways: a loss of C9ORF72 protein, RNA toxicity arising from sequestered RNA binding proteins, and repeat-associated non-AUG-dependent translation of repetitive RNA into toxic dipeptide repeat proteins.    Several approaches, such as antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), duplex or single-stranded siRNAs, miRNAs and small compounds, have been shown to reduce gain-of-toxicity features caused by the G4C2 repeat associated with C9ORF72-ALS. First generation miRNAs addressed the gain of toxic function mechanism underlying the disease, but also further lowered transcript levels to worsen C9ORF72 haploinsufficiency. In contrast, ASOs concomitantly reduce toxic RNA foci and preserve C9 transcript levels. However, multiple injections are required to produce a therapeutic effect; thus, increasing the possibility of adverse effects. Furthermore, ASOs have limited biodistribution in the brain, and are therefore, unlikely to mitigate FTD phenotypes driven by cortical G4C2 repeat expansions. This is important because up to 50% of ALS patients eventually progress to an FTD phenotype. Genethon’s approach combines the use of ASOs (that do not further lower C9ORF72 protein levels) and gene therapy vectors. Excitingly, this approach will overcome the need for recurring ASOs injections and achieve a relatively more widespread distribution throughout the brain.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Pathological aggregation of tau protein characterizes a wide range of neurodegenerative diseases known as tauopathies, including Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) and Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). Interestingly, in several tauopathies, tau pathology progresses under a characteristic temporospatial pattern and in AD the extent of tau pathology correlates with the severity of dementia, suggesting the concept of physical spreading of tau pathology from cell to cell. Multiple causative pathogenic mutations in the MAPT gene identified in FrontoTemporal Dementia with Parkinsonism favor the aggregation of tau in brain. The microtubule binding repeat domain (MTBR) of the tau protein is involved in the aggregation of tau and trancellular propagation of tau pathology. Our objective is to deliver disease-modifying treatment by neutralizing and/or increasing the clearance of soluble pathological tau species to block the progression of tau pathology and slow down the cognitive and motor decline associated with tauopathies, including PSP and AD. Our strategy is optimizing our anti-tau MTBR mAbs with brain penetrant constructs.

The IL-21 pathway is critical for driving IgG production under a normal immune response and we theorize this same pathway will be critical in production of high affinity autoantibodies in an autoimmune disease. . IL-21 deficient patients are primary immune-deficient (PID) with B and T cell deficits with low or below average levels of protective IgG and diminished T-dependent immune responses.  Further aspects of the innate system are negatively effected demonstrating the potential of blockade of the pathway in an autoimmune patient to reign in these aspects of dysregulation driving the respective autoimmune pathology.  . To this end, Novo Nordisk ran a clinical trial with an anti-IL-21 antibody.  They concluded that blockade resulted in clinical efficacy in RA.  Importantly their were no significant safety findings reported in this study.. Beside the trial data, the literature supports targeting IL-21 pathway for RA and multiple other autoimmune diseases discussed at length in our proposal document.  Pathway blockade positively impacts multiple disease models.  We endeavor to make a fully human anti-IL-21 directed, neutralizing antibody for the treatment of autoimmune diseases like RA and SLE. We have designed a screening cascade and antibody generation strategy that will support this antibody development, testing in relevant animal models and appropriate in vitro screens. In parallel to the antibody campaign we will be working with patient samples to better characterize specific cell phenotypes, cytokine levels such as IL-21 and gene signatures indicative of activation of IL-21 dependent genes to support a strong patient centric credentialing of this pathway to test our theories of mechanism of action and develop biomarkers that will instruct target patient populations within heterogeneous diseases like RA and SLE among others.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Galanin is a 29-30 amino acid neuropeptide, widely distributed in the central and peripheral nervous systems. Galanin modulates a variety of physiological processes including feeding, nociception, nerve regeneration, memory, neuroendocrine release, gut secretion and contractility. The receptors mediating these actions are galanin receptors (subtypes 1, 2, 3). GALR1 is predominantly expressed in the central and peripheral nervous systems and at lower levels in the peripheral tissues. GALR2 is more widely distributed in peripheral tissues with a high expression in the human digestive system. GALR3 expression is low in both central and peripheral tissues. Recently, a new peptide SQT44227 (today published as spexin) has been characterized by TIB as a new ligand for the GALR2 and GALR3. SQT4427 is relatively specific for the hGALR3, with weaker affinity for hGALR2 (120-fold) and no binding observed for hGALR1. SQT4427 is therefore an endogenous ligand that preferentially binds the Gal3 receptors, whereas galanin is relatively non-selective. Spexin activates GalR3 in a MAPK assay (based on luciferase read out) with an EC50 ~30nM versus ~1µM only for galanin. This functional activation can be inhibited by three GALR3 antagonist reference compounds (SR244400 SR153681 SSR107528A). A first lead (A00345397/new chemical series) from MTS screening (100k SASC1) has been characterized as spexin antagonist for GALR3 (MAPK assay / IC50 ~350nM). Therefore, this assay using Spexin is a useful secondary functional assay for testing GALR3 leads.  #  It remained the question of the physiological functions of this new characterized ligand for GalR2/3. A working hypothesis is expected from co-expression studies (mRNA/protein) between Spexin and its targets (GALR2/3).

TARGET_RATIONALE: Kv1.3 is a potassium selective voltage gated ion channel expressed in lymphocytes and other tissues. Kv1.3 is selectively upregulated in pathologically relevant activated effector memory T cells (TEM cells). Channel function is essential for sustained Ca2+ entry and cytokine expression in TEM cells. Inhibition of Kv1.3 using potent peptide blockers has been shown to improve outcomes in several animal models of autoimmunity such as pristane-induced arthritis and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis. The most advanced Kv1.3 blocking peptide Dalazitide showed efficacy signals but also neurological side effects in a PhIb clinical trial. This indicates that more potent/selective inhibition of Kv1.3 by an anti-Kv1.3. nanobody or a bispecific nanobody combining anti-Kv1.3 with an additional TEM-targeted moiety may achieve clinically important and safe suppression of autoimmune responses in patients.

Chagas disease is caused by infection with the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, which is transmitted by an insect vector (Triatomines), or acquired orally after consuming contaminated food, congenitally, or via blood transfusions and organ transplantation.. Chagas is a devastating disease affecting 10-20 million people in Latin America. In recent years, the substantial migration of Latin Americans to Europe and North America has brought significant numbers of infected individuals. Screening for Chagas in blood and organ donations is now performed routinely in most of these countries. Unfortunately, treatment of infected subjects is not routine. In total, 100 million people are at risk worldwide.. There are few immediate prospects for vaccines to prevent human Chagas disease and a large number of infected subjects will themselves develop clinical disease or will serve as sources of infection for others. There are two main drugs available for acute Chagas disease. These were developed >40 years ago and come with various drawbacks: Nifurtimox (Lampit® Bayer), a nitrofuran and Benznidazole, (Rochagan®, Radanil®, Roche) a nitroimidazole derivative, are reported to have high cure rates in those with acute infection but NO activity in chronic disease. In truth their efficacy in either stage is unknown due to the lack of reliable methods to assess the persistence of infection. Promising leads for anti-T. cruzi compounds have been identified but few, including those currently in or planned for clinical trials in humans, have been tested for the ability to provide sterile clearance. However, sterile clearance is an essential characteristic that a new anti-Chagas disease medicine should have, since chronic disease, as mentioned above, represents the greatest health and economic burden of Chagas. In this project, we propose to take advantage of the multiple excellent animal systems for assessing parasitological cure and the technical advances recently made for determining treatment efficacy for pre-clinical evaluation of candidate compounds.. The cost of production of compounds is another important issue in any neglected disease and in Chagas in particular. The compounds planned for clinical trials in Chagas disease at the moment may remain inaccessible to the populations in greatest need because of their high cost of production.
