By converting AMP into adenosine, CD73 (HUGO symbol: NT5E) is a key regulator of the proinflammatory and anti-inflammatory balance of purines in the extracellular milieu. Adenosine generated by CD73 expressed on barrier cell types (endothelia, epithelia) is implicated in the control of a variety of physiologic responses, including regulation of endothelial permeability, vascular leakage, attenuation of neutrophil adhesion, epithelial ion and fluid transport. CD73 expression is regulated by HIF1alpha. It is also defined as a lymphocyte differentiation antigen, and is thought to function as a co-signaling molecule on T lymphocytes, and as an adhesion molecule that is important for lymphocyte binding to endothelium.. CD73 expression on Treg contributes to Treg immunosuppressive functions. CD73 was shown to be expressed on tumor cells in several cancer types, where it would promote tumor immune escape. CD73 is expressed on EC and prevents T cell adhesion to and migration through endothelium.. In vivo, pharmacological blockade of CD73 inhibits tumor growth and metastasis. TARGET_RATIONALE: FGFR3 is one of many physiological regulators of linear growth. It normally functions as an inhibitor, acting negatively on both proliferation and terminal differentiation of growth plate chondrocytes. . The FGFR3 mutations associated with chondrodysplasias can be classified in three main categories: extracellular, transmembrane and intracellular tyrosine kinase domain mutations. Based on the prevalence of the different chondrodysplasias and the frequency of the specific mutations, about 55% of patients have mutations in the transmembrane domain, 25% in the extracellular domain and ~20% in the intracellular kinase domain ] Kinase domain FGFR3 mutations increase catalytic activity independently of receptor dimerization by disengaging the molecular brake at the kinase hinge region.. Several mouse models with knock-in FGFR3 mutations have been generated to recapitulate the human disease. These animals show a narrowing of the growth plates of vertebrae and long bones, a decrease in the height of proliferative and hypertrophic zones of the growth plate as well as an overall dwarf phenotype. Therefore, inhibition or attenuation of FGFR3 signaling in the growth plate should correct the skeletal abnormalities characteristic of the disease.. Although FGFR3 is broadly expressed, its actions are specific to the chondrocytes regulating endochondral bone growth. This is evident by Fgfr3 null mice where homozygous mice are viable, and the major phenotype observed is skeletal overgrowth. In addition, it has been shown that FGFR3 gene is not essential for embryonic or postnatal survival.

One of the most common oncogenic EGFR mutations is an extracellular truncation of the EGFR known as the de27 EGFR, which is frequently expressed in glioma. This truncation results in the removal of 267 amino acids from the extracellular domain of the EGFR. So RAMP2 represents a potential target for pro-angiogenic drugs.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Autoimmune diseases cause severe disability and chronic pain, and they lead to considerable socio-economic costs. Current treatment options are in most cases not really curative, and often have a high percentage of non-responders. Thus, innovative therapeutic options against autoimmune diseases are urgently required. Accumulating evidence suggests that changes in the metabolism of immune cells significantly contribute to the pathogenesis of autoimmunity, and different autoimmune diseases appear to share alterations in metabolic pathways, key metabolites or metabolic byproducts. Examples for metabolic changes in autoimmune settings include modifications in amino acid and cholesterol levels or glucose catabolism or ROS. Thus, the emerging field of immunometabolism may hold the potential to discover new therapeutic targets. CD109 is a glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)anchored cell surface glycoprotein and is a member of the α2-macroglobulin-C3, C4, and C5 family of thioester-containing proteins. CD109 expression in normal tissues appears to be restricted to limited cells, including myoepithelial cells (breast, salivary, lacrimal, bronchial secretary glands, basal cells of the prostate), endothelial cells, activated but not resting T lymphocytes, activated but no resting platelets, leukemic megakaryoblast and a subset of gated CD34+ cells on adults and foetal bone marrow. CD109 expression is upregulated in squamous cell carcinomas of the lung, esophagus, uterus and oral cavity. CD109 is a TGF beta accessory/auxiliary receptors. Its overexpression decreases TGF-β1-induced phosphorylation of Smad2 and Smad3, and impaired the TGFβ1 mediated supression of cell proliferation, differentiation, migration, and extracellular matrix deposition. It has been proposed  that CD109 overexpression in premalignant lesions inhibits the antiproliferative effects of the TGF-β signal and contributes to tumor development. CD109 is a target coming from the CD105 phenotypic screening on endothelial cells (LC80414). The objective of the screening was to find original targets inhibiting angiogenesis by maintaining endothelial cells with a quiescent phenotype.

TARGET_RATIONALE: PDE10 is a dual-substrate (cAMP and cGMP) phosphodiesterase expressed mainly in brain (putamen, caudate nucleus) and testis and much less in other organs (kidney, heart). Expression is also detected in certain endocrine cell types (pituitary, thyroid, adrenal glands, Langerhans islets).  #  The involvement of PDE10 in the control of the striatal output from medium spiny neurons is well documented in the literature. PDE10 inhibitors increase cGMP and cAMP levels in the striatum in vivo and potentiate the striatal output induced by dopamine / glutamate. PDE10 inhibitors potentiate catalepsy induced by the dopamine D2 receptor antagonist haloperidol in rat. They also inhibit the hyperlocomotion induced by the NMDA receptor antagonist phencyclidine in rat and conditioned avoidance responding in mice. This indicates PDE10 inhibitors could be therapeutically useful in the treatment of neurological and psychiatric disorders that involve dysfunction of the basal ganglia (psychosis, schizophrenia, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, obsessive-compulsive disorder, addiction, ...).  #  In Beta cells of the pancreas, PDE10 appears to play a key role in the control of cAMP levels. By increasing intracellular cAMP levels, PDE10 inhibitors could potentiate the action of a number of endogenous secretagogues (such as GLP-1, GIP, PACAP, VIP) that utilize the cAMP system to regulate insulin secretion in a glucose-dependent fashion. PDE10 inhibition would result in increased insulin release at high glucose level only and thereby have a beneficial antidiabetic effect.  #  PDE10 KO mice exhibit reduced spontaneous locomotor activity and, when exposed to a high-fat diet, are resistant to developing increase in body weight / adiposity and symptoms of metabolic syndrome, pointing to a critical role of PDE10 both in CNS (regulation of striatal function) and metabolism of fat and glucose.

Lymphotoxin Beta receptor functions as a receptor for the heterodimer of lymphotoxin-alpha and lymphotoxin-beta. It is expressed on the surface of most cell types including cells of epithelial and myeloid lineages. It plays a role in the development and organization of lymphoid tissues and stimulation of LTbR on dendritic cells has been shown to be critical for their homeostasis and expansion. Signaling via LTbR also been shown to induce the death of some adenocarcinoma cell lines (probably via TRAF3 and TRAF5). A region in the CRD1 domain of some TNFR-like receptors can self-associate = PLAD (Pre-Ligand Assembly Domain). This allows the assembly (di- or tri-merization) of the receptors in the absence of ligand, through a distinct domain from the ligand binding site, and thus promotes receptor function. Despite structural similarities, strong differences in amino acid sequences of CRD1 for TNFR-like receptors. The purpose is to select small selective molecules capable of inhibiting the pre-oligomerization of the receptor LTbR (through interaction with the PLAD domain) and therefore block the signaling and cell responses induced by this receptor.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Medicinal uses of Calendula officinalis extracts
TARGET_RATIONALE: Calendula officinalis or Marigold has a wide geographic distribution with extensive ethnobotanical use history for treating GI disorders, minor skin wounds, sun burn eczema, skin cancer, ear infections.  It has been given GRAS (generally regarded as safe status) by the FDA for use as a spice, natural seasoning and for flavoring.  Calendula is used in almost 200 cosmetic applications with a good safety profile based on animal LD 50 values / minimal skin irritation or sensitization reported for topical applications. The principal identified constituents are triterpenoids and flavonoids, carotenoids, auroxanthins. There is no well known standard extraction method and overall the chemistry is viewed as complex (room for novelty).  Calendula extracts are reported as active in animal wound healing models and also been shown to have effects on wound healing mechanisms of relevance (anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidant, anti-bacterial/-viral, with enhanced fibroblast proliferation and collagen production). A Calendula extract has shown encouraging results in a venous leg ulcer trial and one was being evaluated for treating dermatitis pain and erythema during radiation therapy.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Rett syndrome, a severe neurological disorder affecting about 1 in 10,000 girls is caused by a spontaneous mutation in a single gene on the X chromosome, that encodes the protein methyl-CPG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2). AAV mediated combination of suppression + replacement (in concert) therapy has been shown to be of benefit in several models of RHO-adRP. (23), 2012 and Greenwald et al., Gen. Ther. (1), 2013); Mussolino et al., EMBO Mol Med., 2011) targeted to the mutated RHO transgene. Muscle function/strength is the most relevant physiological parameter compromised in muscle wasting states, and functional impairment is invariantly linked to loss of muscle mass. Muscle mass depends on the balance of protein synthesis and degradation, and there is ample evidence in literature that muscle anabolic pathways are compromised in human disuse atrophy and sarcopenia. The cellular mechanisms involved in decreased muscle function are diverse and include an increase in catabolic processes, a loss/dysfunction of motor neurons, decreased muscle cell functionality, defects in excitation-contraction coupling, an altered fiber composition, and mitochondrial dysfunction. The relative contribution of these processes depends on the underlying (patho)-physiology (aging, muscle disuse, chronic disease), the muscle type, and also on the species. Meanwhile, several muscle anabolic approaches e. g. testosterone or analogs, IGF-1, GH, amino acid supplementation, or �-agonists have demonstrated efficacy in increasing muscle mass in animal models as well as in humans. However, the above listed anabolic principles still suffer from severe side effects and safety issues, thus necessitating the search for safe treatment options that will enable their use in elderly patients suffering from diverse muscle wasting disorders and disuse atrophy as consequence of immobilization.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Adrenomedullin (AM) is a small peptide of 52 aa that binds and signals through a GPCR, the calcitonin receptor-like receptor (CRLR). The ligand-binding affinity of CRLR is determined via receptor interaction with a class of single-pass transmembrane proteins called receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMPs). RAMP2 and RAMP3 complexed with CRLR form high-affinity AM receptors. The system AM/CRLR/RAMP2 plays an essential role in angiogenesis and vascular integrity. Indeed, RAMP2-null, CRLR-null or AM-null embryos died at mid-gestation due to vascular fragility that led to severe edema and lymphedema with hemorrhages. Vascular endothelial cells in RAMP2-null embryos are severely deformed and detached from the basement membrane leading to paracellular leakage and contributing to the edema observed. So RAMP2 represents a potential target for pro- or anti-angiogenic drugs in cancer and rheumatoid arthritis.

P66Shc is a mitochondrial protein with redox activity involved in ROS generation and apoptotic processes. It is activated by phosphorylation upon oxidative stress and translocated to the mitochondrial intermembrane space where it oxidizes cytochrome c, leading to ROS generation, mitochondria depolarization and apoptosis. Mitochondrial dysfunction is involved in a variety of renal diseases, including acute kidney injury, through excessive production of ROS. Involvement of p66Shc in mitochondrial dysfunction has been demonstrated in renal proximal tubular cells during oxidative injury, suggesting a potential role of p66Shc in AKI. This hypothesis is supported by our in-house data showing a clear activation of p66shc in three different rodent AKI models.

Centella asiatica common name Indian Pennywort, Gotu Kola small perennial creeping plant growing in moist areas throughout southeast Asia. Has a long history dating back to ancient Chinese and Ayurvedic medicine traditionally used to treat chronic venus insufficiency, wound healing, mental disorders, atherosclerosis, as fungicide, as antibacterial, antioxidant, anti cancer, for burns, treating leprosy, lupus, psoriasis, keloid scars and in preventing ulcers.  Active ingredients are reported to be 3 triterpenes - asiatic acid, madecassic acid and asiaticoside.  It has been reported that asiaticoside is rapidly converted to asiatic acid in vivo which is believed to be the most therapeutically active ingredient.  Several studies show Centella's ability to improve wound healing with some aspects of the chemical compounds in the herb reported to aid scar treatment as well.    Asiaticoside/asiatic acid have been shown to inhibit expression or production of TGf-beta, TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta, PGE2, COX-2, extracellular matrix proteins, to inhibit NF-Kappa B activation and induce expression of TG-beta pathway inhibitor Smad7.  These effects have been demonstrated in vitro and in vivo.  In guinea pig punch wounds topical application of 0.2% solution of asiaticoside produced 56% increase in hydroxyproline, 57% increase in wound tensile strength, increased collagen content and better epithelisation.  In streptozotocin in diabetic rats, where healing is delayed, topical application of 0.4% solution asiaticoside over punch wounds had similar effects thus promoting healing in an accepted model of diabetic ulcer healing.  Asiaticoside has been shown to be active by the oral route also 1mg/kg in a guinea pig punch model.  In summary the chemical components of Centella appear to promote cell proliferation and collagen synthesis, the faster maturation and cross linking of collagen and increasing the aldehyde content thus improving tensile strength.  Additionally Centella extract appears to possess anti-inflammatory, as well as anti-bacterial properties and asiaticoside has also been shown to promote angiogenesis (promoting neovascularization) .  The positive effects of C.asiatica in wound healing are convincing and supported by numerous published scientific reports. There is also emerging evidence to support its use for the improvement of scars (citations by cosmetic surgeons) especially keloid scars.  The botanical is thus supported for wound healing indications.

EXPLO project EU0053: Regeneration is generally considered to be a phenomenon restricted to amphibians, in which amputated limbs reform and regrow. In the adult newt and in the axolotl, the replacement of limbs begins with the formation of a blastema, a structure with highly proliferative cells that grow until that appendage is replaced without scarring. On the other hand, mammals typically heal wounds by the process of repair, characterized by wound site contraction and closure with a scar. The adult MRL mouse strain is able to regenerates appendage tissues (i.e. regeneration of digit tips after amputation, cardiac lesion, close ear holes induced by ear punching). This ability is probably due to a distinct cell-cycle (G2/M accumulation) phenotype of MRL?s fibroblast-like cells in which  the p53-target p21 (regulator-gene of G1 checkpoint) is not expressed. p21 KO mice, as well as MRL mice, close ear holes induced by ear punching, shown a G2/M accumulation and increased in cellular  apoptosis, providing a firm link between p21 gene and tissue regeneration. Aim of the project is to study p21 site-specific inactivation (i.e. use of small molecules) through the use of murine wound healing models (ear punching model, wound healing model) and cellular models, to validate its implication in regenerative capabilities, in order to find pharmacological tools able to modulate p21 expression, as new approach on regenerative medicine with particular attention on the healing of the scars and the chronic skin ulcers.

Frizzled 7 (FZD7) is a member of the seven-transmembrane Wnt receptor family (FZD1- FZD10) that translates extracellular Wnt signals into intracellular changes in gene expression. The Wnt signaling pathway regulates numerous cellular processes including cell differentiation, migration, proliferation and embryonic development.  From this broad list of processes regulated by Wnt, signaling through the FZD7receptor is more specifically involved in muscle satellite cell expansion, stem cell pluripotency and cancer metastasis. . FZD7 is expressed in quiescent muscle satellite stem cells and is upregulated in proliferating satellite cell and myoblasts. Signaling of Wnt7a through FZD7, along the non-canonical Wnt pathway, induces expansion of the satellite stem cell population.  In primary mouse myofibers, knockdown of FZD7 prevented Wnt7a from stimulating symmetric satellite cell division. Symmetric cell division is required for expansion of the satellite stem cell population.                . An agonist monoclonal antibody directed against FZD7 would be expected to act like the natural Wnt7a ligand in muscle satellite stem cells to promotes expansion of the satellite stem cell population. The proposed therapeutic should be useful in treating age-related muscle degeneration, musculoskeletal disorders, and wound healing by promoting expansion of satellite stem cells and muscle hypertrophy.

The adaptive immune system communicates with the innate immune system  to promote inflammation using IL-17. The expression of IL-17 has been reported in patients with RA, MS, lupus and asthma.  Biotherapeutic approaches are currently being deployed to targeting IL-17 and its receptor preclinically and clinically.  Based on all this information it is hypothesized that a small molecule inhibitor of IL-17 production will be efficacious in the treatment of auto immune diseases like RA, asthma and MS.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Internal transcriptomic studies have identified  the activin receptor ALK7 (HUGO symbol: ACVR1C), a Ser/Thr receptor of the TGFb superfamily, as upregulated in the rat hippocampus during the early stages of epileptogenesis. This phenomenon is selective to Alk7 and does not affect the other activin receptor, Alk4. The kinetic of Alk7 regulation parallels that of the well known epilepsy players NPY and BDNF. In addition, Activin AB, Alk7 ligand, and Smad3, through which Alk7 signalizes, are also upregulated at the same stages. The activin pathway is known to play an important role during neuronal development and is more and more described for its role in the CNS. In the adult brain, it likely regulates long-term synaptic changes in highly excitable brain regions (hippocampus, amygdala). Taken all together, these data support ALK7 as a potential innovative disease-modifier target for epilepsy. On the other way, literature and internal (antidepressant transcriptomic projects) studies suggest that activin pathway may represent an interesting target for anxiety/depression as well. In particular, it was demonstrated that activation of activin receptors in the hippocampus induces antidepressant like effects. Therefore, selective activators for Alk7 receptors could also represent new anti-depressant compounds with an innovative mechanism of action.

TARGET_RATIONALE: PRPF4B (PRP4 pre-mRNA processing factor 4 homolog B) is a dual-specificity protein kinase that was identified in the TRAIL modulators RNAi screen.  Knock-down of PRPF4B, using either siRNAs or lentivirus-encoded shRNAs, was found to sensitize liquid tumor cell lines to apoptosis in response to low-dose TRAIL stimulation.  Moreover, liquid tumor cell lines stably transduced with shRNAs against PRPF4B displayed reduced survival in culture relative to either non-transduced cells or to cells transduced with shRNAs incapable of mediating PRPF4B knockdown.  PRPF4B mRNA expression is upregulated not only in liquid tumor cell lines (relative to non-transformed PBMCs), but also in hematological malignancy cells isolated from patients with NHL, CLL, follicular lymphoma, and AML. There are few publications on the function of PRPF4B in mammalian cells.  It was identified in S. pombe as a temperature-sensitive pre-mRNA processing mutant, a defect that was reversed by substitution of the kinase domain of human PRPF4B.  PRPF4B has been shown to bind and phosphorylate SF2, a splicing factor recently characterized as a proto-oncogene.  Interestingly, our analysis of gene profiling databases containing 71 different primary and in vitro liquid tumor samples revealed that SF2 is the most closely correlated gene to PRPF4B at the level of mRNA expression.  We hypothesize that PRPF4B overexpression in liquid tumor cells unmasks the oncogenic, pro-survival activity of SF2 (and possibly other downstream targets).  Therefore, we seek to identify inhibitors of PRPF4B that can be used as novel, first-in-class therapeutics to treat liquid tumors, by a proposed mechanism that involves attacking the aberrant alternative splicing events associated with liquid tumor progression.  We propose to perform HTS with E.coli-purified PRPF4B kinase domain, as this has been shown to have intrinsic activity in vitro, without requiring phosphorylation by an upstream activator.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Start: 2015-05-26. new target: RETNLB (RELM-beta)
TARGET_RATIONALE: Resistin-like molecule β (RELMβ) is a proinflammatory hormone secreted primarily by goblet cells of the intestines and lungs. Recent studies have found that its production and secretion can be induced by a broad range of stimuli, including pathogens, proinflammatory cytokines, nutrients, and insulin, and that chronic overproduction can lead to a chronic low-grade inflammation that can promote diabetes, atherosclerosis, cancer, and other diseases. Evidence for the relationship between RELMβ and disease has been seen in many animal models where the administration or overexpression of RELMβ leads to altered glucose homeostasis, insulin resistance, hyperlipidemia, and NASH, and where knocking out the RELMβ gene confers protection from conditions such as colitis, lung fibrosis, and atherosclerosis. Similarly, evidence is being gathered for the role of RELMβ in human pathologies, where increased expression has been seen in atherosclerotic plaques and in intestinal tract cancers.. With this project, we aim to investigate the feasibility of developing a therapeutic molecule that can neutralize RELMβ (e.g., an anti-RELMβ mAb) or antagonize its receptor (e.g., a small-molecule antagonist). Since the receptor for RELMβ is not known, and no robust assays exist to screen for neutralizing antibodies in vitro, we propose to take a three-step approach to initiating a drug discovery program for RELMβ. First, we will identify the receptor protein using receptor finding technologies developed by Protosera Inc. Second, in collaboration with Professor Asano at Hiroshima University, we will generate and test cells expressing the receptor to validate its identity as a bona fide receptor for RELMβ and to develop assays that can detect the functional interaction between the receptor and RELMβ. And third, based on our better understanding of the relevant cells and signaling pathways of RELMβ that come from our work on the receptor, we will work together with TSU Diabetes and TSU Oncology to develop a plan to screen for molecules that block the interaction. . It is anticipated that a successful identification and validation of the RELMβ receptor will lead to a decision point in early 2016 to initiate drug screening. After potent blocking molecules are found, Professor Asano will be prepared to help to test the efficacy of the molecules in vivo using his RELMβ-humanized mouse models of disease.

SREB is a subfamily of G-protein-coupled receptors, which consists of SREB1 (GPR27), SREB2 (GPR85), and SREB3 (GPR173). Its high evolutionary conservation and predominant expression in the CNS suggest that SREB family members and their undiscovered ligand(s) may have significant functions in the nervous system. GPR27 shares the highest sequence similarity with amine GPCRs, such as ADRB3 and 5HT2C. In house and public data show high neuronal expression in with brain structures known to possess high levels of plasticity such as the hippocampal formation. Therefore all SREB receptors, including GPR27, represent potential targets for neurology (Alzheimer, epilepsy) and Psychiatry (Schizophrenia, Depression) diseases. GPR27 was also found to be upregulated in hearts of congestive heart failure patients as well as in kidneys of patients with diabetic nephropathy, indicating a putative pathophysiological role in cardio-renal diseases.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Aminoglycosides constitute an historical, well validated class of naturally occurring antibiotics with activities vs enterobacteriaceae and Gram(+) but generally poorly active on pseudomonas. The corresponding biosynthetic gene clusters will be then transferred to heterologous strains to cleanly produce extracts containing the expected new NPs. Following microbiological testing against a panel of relevant Gram(-), the active extracts will be then dereplicated and the active components isolated for structure elucidation and confirmation of activity. TARGET_RATIONALE: Opioids are widely used throughout the world to treat clinical pain. Opioid analgesics produce their potent analgesic effects by activating mu, delta, or kappa opioid receptors. Morphine is the gold standard of this therapeutic class but, as other opioids, is not effective in the treatment of all types of chronic pain. In addition, opioids and morphine present a lot of unwanted side-effects, particularly constipation, respiratory and cardiovascular depression, histamine release, pruritus and metabolite accumulation. M6G is one of the active metabolites of morphine. Its analgesic activity has been demonstrated more potent than morphine itself but its accumulation leads to neurological effects and potentially life-threatening overdose. M6G presents in its chemical structure a carboxylic moiety (glucuronide) which potentially could be replaced with carboxylic acid mimics that could be able to give rise to compounds as efficient as M6G but with a better safety profile. Some preliminary results (in collaboration with Francopia and Sanofi-Chimie) suggest that some heterocycles can replace the acidic function of M6G leading to potent analgesics in vivo. The summary report is available on request to Pascal GEORGE.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Protein kinase CK2 is distributed ubiquitously in eukaryotic organisms, where it most often appears to exist in tetrameric complexes consisting of two catalytic subunits (alpha and/or alpha prime chains) and two regulatory subunits (beta chains).  The alpha, alpha prime and beta chains are encoded by the CSNK2A1, CSNK2A2 and CSNK2B genes respectively. The catalytic chains are constitutively active, and depending on the protein substrates, the beta chain may or may not regulate the specificity of the enzyme.  #  CK2 has a somewhat unique ability to utilize GTP (Km ~ 20 microM) as a phosphate donor in place of ATP (Km ~ 10 microM). In the presence of Mg2+, ATP is the more efficient substrate but in the presence of Mn2+, the situation is reversed (Gatica et al, 1993).  #  Protein kinase CK2 is oncogenic. Targeted expression of CK2 alpha in T cells and in mammary glands of transgenic mice leads to lymphomagenesis and mammary tumorigenesis respectively (Landesman-Bollag et al, 2001). CK2 alpha transgenic mice partially or completely deficient in p53 develop thymic lymphomas at a markedly accelerated rate when compared to p53-deficient mice lacking the transgene (Landesman-Bollag et al, 1998). Oncogenic co-operativity was also shown with c-Myc, tal-1 and H-RAS in different systems.  #  Protein kinase CK2 is overexpressed in colon, breast, prostate, lung, head & neck, and kidney cancers. Elevated protein kinase CK2 activity is associated with aggressive behavior of squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (Gapany et al, 1995). CK2 is a predictor of survival in lung squamous cell carcinoma patients (O-charoenrat et al, 2004). Multiple myeloma cell survival relies on high activity of protein kinase CK2 alpha (Piazza et al, 2006). Nuclear localization of CK2 alpha is associated with poor prognostic factors in human prostate cancer (Laramas et al, 2007). Protein Kinase CK2 alpha is an unfavorable prognostic marker in AML (Kim et al, 2007).  #  Protein kinase CK2 is involved in resistance to apoptosis induced by TRAIL, Fas, and TNF-alpha.  #  Protein kinase CK2 is involved in drug resistance (Etoposide, Doxorubicin, 6-thioguanine, Resveratrol, EGCG, etc).  #  Protein kinase CK2 inhibits the activation of caspases, and activates NF-kappaB, WNT and PI3K pathways.  #  In oncology disease group, we have recently shown that CK2 siRNA knock down induced apoptosis in HCT116 cell line.

In animal studies, Salvia commonly known Danshen appeared to interfere with the development of liver fibrosis - the formation of scar-like fibers in the liver. Because the non-functioning fibers crowd out active liver tissue, liver function decreases gradually as the amount of fibrous tissue increases. Having chronic hepatitis and habitually drinking large amounts of alcoholic beverages are the major causes of liver fibrosis, which could also result from exposure to chemicals or certain drugs. Danshen may also increase blood flow into the liver, so the length of time that potentially damaging substances stay in the liver may be reduced, also reducing the possible injury they may cause. Results from a few animal studies show that it may also protect kidney tissues from damage caused by diabetes. In China, danshen has also been studied for treating acute pancreatitis, painful and possibly dangerous inflammation of the pancreas.   Key active components appear to be Tanshinone and Cryptotanshinone. Key data of relevance to liver fibrosis includes. a) salvia extracts are effective in the rat CCL4 model, in a therapeutic setting. b) Activity in rat hepatic stellate cells shown with active components (Sal B and TashinoneIIA) - Salvia has been assigned for liver fibrosis indication.

Recognition that neglected tropical diseases due to human helminth infection contribute greatly to the cycle of poverty that plagues poor regions of the world has spurred recent investment in the identification of new and better drugs to control or eliminate these pathogens. None of the anthelmintics used in humans can be considered "optimal", especially in the context of Mass Drug Administration, although their deployment has led to undeniable gains in controlling the pathology and transmission of these infections. A few drugs that have been developed and registered for uses in veterinary medicine or for other human infections may have applications for helminthiases, but new drugs are still needed. Early discovery pipelines for these diseases are not robust, and renewed efforts at lead identification and development are necessary for sustainable control and potential elimination of these pathogens. The lack of acute lethality associated with helminthiases has limited investment in drug discovery targeted to them, even in comparison with malaria, tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS. They are truly neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) which place an enormous burden on global health.. Chemotherapy remains the only strategy available to treat helminth infections of humans. Marketed drugs label extension and translational informatics will be used as strategy to address these infections.. The project will be done in partnership with DNDi and in alignment with A2M. TARGET_RATIONALE: Rationale:  ALS is a neuromuscular disorder characterized by the loss of neurons that innervate and control muscle. The loss of motor neurons leads to progressive muscular weakness, paralysis and ultimately death due to respiratory failure. The demise of motor neurons is triggered by neighboring cells, which secrete an unknown toxic entity. Sphingolipids are structural membrane components that have bioactive roles in a number of processes affected by ALS including metabolism, myelination, neuroinflammation and pathways of cell death. Several lines of evidence suggest that accumulation of ceramide, the fundamental building block of all sphingolipids, contributes to motor neuron degeneration. For example, genetic mutations that result in the impaired lysosomal degradation of ceramide lead to motor neuron disease in humans.  Furthermore, we observed elevated ceramide levels in the spinal cords of sporadic ALS patients and ALS mice. Excitingly, we have also recently determined that surrounding neighboring cells are the source of pathogenic ceramide levels through secretion of sphingosine. Secreted sphingosine enters mitochondria of motor neurons to trigger their death.  Indeed, sphingosine is elevated in the spinal cords of ALS patients and ALS mice (Dodge at al). Interestingly, mitochondrial toxicity (in other cellular models of disease) triggered by sphingosine is dependent up the enzyme ceramide synthase 6 (Cers6). The epidemic increase in obese humans worldwide is followed by a similar increase in diabetes and cardiovascular diseases.  Such patients are particularly prone to the development of chronic wounds which become colonized by a number of bacterial species.  Bacterial colonization alone does not delay the wound healing process and in most individuals may actually be beneficial however colonization may transition rapidly to invasion / infection in individuals with poor local factors (arterial insufficiency, venous hypertension, trauma or systemic disease (diabetes, RA).   Recently there is increasing evidence that bacteria within chronic, non-healing wounds live within biofilm communities characterized by diverse microbial flora, adhering to each other and the wound surface, embedded within a self-produced matrix of extracellular polymeric substance.   Bacteria within this biofilm are able to communicate, regulate their metabolic states, the release of endotoxins and are well protected from host defenses, developing resistance to antibiotic treatment.   It has been suggested that chronicity in wounds begins with a persistent tissue level of bacteria, in particular endotoxin production, resulting in prolonged elevation of pro-inflammatory cytokines ultimately resulting in an excessive, continuing inflammatory response causing the repair process to become stalled.. This pre-program aims to identify botanical extracts with broad spectrum anti-microbial properties or specific anti-biofilm directed activities (quorum sensing inhibition, anti-adhesion, pro-dispersion).  Herbal Extracts will initially be identified from the literature and subsequently tested in vitro through a collaborative arrangement with TSU ID.   Identified actives will be considered as possible combination partners to be added to a multi-botanical wound healing product topically applied to patient's wounds post surgical debridement, with the specific role to inhibit biofilm reformation.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Legumain (HUGO symbol: LGMN) is an acidic cysteine endopeptidase with restricted specificity, requiring an asparagine at the P1 site of its substrate sequence. Legumain is expressed as a proenzyme and needs acidic conditions for autoprocessing and activation. The gene encoding this asparaginyl endopeptidase was found to be upregulated in many murine and human tumor tissues but absent or present only at very low levels in all normal tissues from which such tumors arise. Importantly, legumain is heavily overexpressed by tumor associated macrophages (TAMs with M2 phenotype) in murine breast tumor tissues. In contrast, classical macrophages of the M1 phenotype, which perform key immune-surveillance and antigen-presentation functions, do not express legumain. Legumain has been suggested to play a role in immunosuppression by cleavage of peptides recognized by cytotoxic T cells. Consequently, inhibition of legumain may be an interesting way to target TAMs without interference with M1 macrophages.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Bradykinin (BK) and the related peptide kallidin (KD or lys-BK) are formed from high and low molecular weight kininogen precursors following the activation of plasma and tissue kallikreins by pathophysiological stimuli such as tissue damage, inflammation or anoxia. The biological actions of kinins are terminated by degradation by several enzymes. Kininase I liberates the major active metabolites [des-Arg9]-BK and [des-Arg10]-KD, whilst kininase II and endopeptidases form inactive metabolites. B2 receptors show a higher affinity for BK and KD, whilst B1 receptors show a higher affinity towards the metabolites [des-Arg9]-BK and [des-Arg10]-KD. In contrast to B2 receptors, which are constitutively expressed on most cell types, B1 receptors are not present in tissues under 'normal' conditions but are induced by inflammatory insults.There is compelling evidence indicating that kinins are rapidly generated after tissue injury and they seem to modulate most of the events observed during the inflammatory processes including vasodilatation, increase of vascular permeability, plasma extravasation, cell migration, pain and hyperalgesia. Moreover, kinins seem to be directly implicated in neurogenic inflammatory events through activation of C-fibers and consequent production of neuropeptides such as substance P and CGRP. Recent evidences suggest a role for BK B2 receptors in acute inflammatory events, whereas B1 receptors appear to be involved in more chronic inflammatory responses. This conclusion is supported by several evidence showing that once the human B1 receptor is expressed, functional responses to ligand stimulation can continue almost indefinitely, because the B1 receptor, unlike B2 subtype, does not desensitize. Furthermore, the receptor can be up-regulated by its own ligand.These findings support other evidence for an involvement of B1 receptors in inflammatory hyperalgesia and suggest that interference with B1 receptor activation may be clinically useful as anti-inflammatory and analgesic drugs. Blocking peptide ligands with antibodies will ameliorate inflammatory and neuropathic nociception and have specificity advantages over small molecule receptor antagonists.

Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death that has been implicated in multiple neurodegenerative diseases. Iron accumulation causes damage to cells by causing lipid peroxidation, a conversion that eventually damages the cell membrane and causes cell death. Iron accumulates in the dentate nucleus of FA patients and the substantia nigra of PD patients and increased iron levels correlate with decreased neuron counts in the substantia nigra of PD patients. Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) is a distant member of the TGF superfamily. It is synthesized as a 308-amino acid polypeptide, and the mature protein is secreted as a disulfide-linked homodimer comprising two 112-amino acid mature regions. Under resting conditions expression of GDF15 is quite low. It gets however upregulated under conditions of cellular stress and can then act as a defense mechanism. In some diseases in which GDF15 is regarded as being protective, such as cancer, chronic kidney disease and heart failure, high serum levels of this protein have been reported. Accordingly, GDF15 is regarded as a biomarker for cancer and cardiorenal diseases.  #  Results from transgenic mice suggest that GDF15 is involved in the physiological control of body weight. While overexpression of GDF15 results in decreased body weight genetic deletion leads to the opposite phenotype. We and others could also show that the administration of recombinant GDF15 improves metabolic health in obese mice by reducing body weight. A recent study identified neurons in the brainstem as being critical for the regulation of food intake and body weight by GDF15. GDF15 is an ideal partner for Fc-GLP-1 as it rescues the body weight effect that seems to be less pronounced with these long-acting GLP-1RA.

ADDITIONAL_PROJECT_INFORMATION: Start: 2017-Sep-27  #  Cluster: Neuroinflammation and MS  #  M0 decision taken on 2017-Sep-15
TARGET_RATIONALE: Project Rationale: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic inflammatory, demyelinating and neurodegenerative disease of the CNS. There is an unmet need for therapies that could provide neuroprotection at all stages of the disease but in particular early in the disease before damage associated with disability can accumulate. The pathophysiological mechanisms leading to axonal damage and neuronal injury are poorly understood but published work suggests that P2X7 plays an important role in neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation and thus represents an attractive target for pharmacological intervention. P2X7 is an ion channel gated by ATP, and its activation leads to a variety of signaling pathways that in many settings leads to the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines and toxins, and also directly promotes cell death. In MS, P2X7 antagonists are hypothesized to inhibit the CNS cells that produce damaging agents (microglia and astrocytes) and provide direct protection to cells that are susceptible to damage (neurons, oligodendrocyte precursor cells [OPCs] and the mature oligodendrocytes [OLs] that normally produce and wrap myelin around axons). The pro-inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress mediators, and other toxins released by microglia and astrocytes following P2X7 activation are key mediators of neuroinflammation and neuronal damage in MS. Furthermore, there is direct genetic evidence linking a rare variant of P2X7, which cannot form inflammatory pores, to protection from MS.  #  Status & Next steps:  We are focused on evaluating CNS penetrant small molecules for targeting this ion channel through a collaboration with Axxam.  Under an initial MTA agreement we accessed two families of small molecules that target P2X7 which Axxam has generated. Using the expertise and assays put in place for the Ablynx P2X7 nanobody collaboration, the team has demonstrated that:  the Axxam small molecules are 1) specific for P2X7, 2) potent on both rodent and human P2X7 channels, 3) active in both rodent microglial and human macrophage cultures, and 4) are CNS penetrant. A collaboration agreement with Axxam was signed in Q3 2017 to extend our data set and analyze Axxam molecules in in vivo experiments as Axxam continues medicinal chemistry work on their P2X7 antagonist molecules. Additionally, we are evaluating reference compounds to compare to Axxam compounds in in vitro and in vivo models. This project transitioned to M0 on September 28, 2017.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Genetic variants of FTO have now been associated in many studies with obesity, insulinoresistance & type2 diabetes. In mice it has recently been shown that inactivation of FTO gene protects from obesity. Variants of FTO have been associated with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in 463 women in a UK study, probably linked to changes in adiposity. In similar study on 263 Rumanian women, clear association of FTO variants with PCOS was found only in obese population.  #  How FTO functions in obesity has not yet been firmly established. Its high level of expression in hypothalamus & some effects on neuropeptide levels in KO mice suggest a role in appetite control. Contradictory data have been presented on regulation of FTO expression in arcuate nucleus of hypothalamus: upregulation by feeding in mice but upregulation by fasting in rats.  #  FTO-/- mice are smaller & lighter, display reduced WAT, increased energy expenditure & increased circulating catecholamine levels. In addition, FTO -/- mice show no difference in food uptake but dietary regime in these experiments is not stated. In contrast, studies on human FTO risk allele do suggest differences in food uptake, particularly in fat uptake. FTO expressed lower levels than in brain in a wide range of peripheral tissues. Studies on FTO risk variant suggest that it may have a role in adipocyte lipolysis. Its role in other metabolically important cell types (pancreatic beta cells, muscle, hepatocytes) has not yet been investigated. FTO is homologous to the DNA repair AlkB protein, a protein that utilizes iron(II), alpha-ketoglutarate & dioxygen to perform oxidative repair of alkylated nucleobases in DNA & RNA and it has been shown that recombinant FTO protein has a similar demethylase activity, acting mainly on 3-methylthymine in single-stranded DNA & 3-methyluracil in single-stranded RNA. The Labège team has shown, using their recombinant FTO, a much higher activity for RNA demethylation than for single-stranded DNA demethylation as analysed by LC/MS. The biological significance of the RNA demethylation activity is not clear for the moment, but it represents a novel type of therap. target.   #  Alternatively, FTO may have yet other demethylase activities that remain to be tested, such as histone demethylation. Histone H3K9-specific demethylation has recently been shown to regulate metabolic gene expression & obesity resistance.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Genetic studies in mice suggested that ablation of CerS6 gene exhibited significantly reduced C16 ceramides in major metabolic tissues and associated with resistance to diet-induced obesity (DIO). First clinical data from Prof Brüning's lab reveals C16 ceramides are involved in the pathogenesis of T2D. Conventionally insulin sensitizers are the front-line therapeutic agents for the newly diagnosed type 2 diabetic patients without risk of hypoglycaemia. However, presently marketed insulin sensitizers suffer with various unmet needs and safety related issues. Consequently, there is an accentuating need for the development of novel insulin sensitizers. CerS6 inhibiton acts as an insulin sensitizer which addresses the root causes of insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. For instance mode of action of these compounds can modify the disease progression rather simply mitigating the syndrome.

Hyperglycemia is a hallmark of type2 diabetes and one of the major causes of diabetes-associated complications. Glucose homeostasis is maintained systemically by hormones such as fasting glucagon & feeding insulin. Jian Zhao (Shanghai Institutes for Biological Sciences (SIBS)) found that a small non-coding RNA microRNA203 (miR203) is the conversion point of fasting & feeding hormone to regulate glucose homeostasis. miR-203 levels are increased by glucagon under fasting, while decreased by insulin during feeding. Overexpression of miR203 suppresses fasting hepatic gluconeogenesis through targeting to CREB1. In parallel, miRNA203 also enhances feeding insulin signaling by suppressing JNK2 & SOCS3. Knockdown of hepatic miR203 expression leads to glucose intolerance, whereas hepatic miR203 overexpression promotes insulin sensitivity. By reciprocal regulation of miR203 expression, fasting & feeding hormones thus trigger a feedback response that maintains glucose homeostasis. Most importantly, miR203 expression is regulated in db/db mouse model of type 2 diabetes & in vivo supplement of miR-203 by adenovirus or specific oligonucleotide mimics ameliorates the insulin resistance syndrome in these mice. Their findings reveal miR203 as a valid target of type 2 diabetes & offer therapeutic intervention in this setting.

TARGET_RATIONALE: Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a histological lesion affecting the kidney glomerulus that causes nephrotic syndrome. There is a high unmet medical need for a therapy for FSGS: steroids are the first line treatment, but 45-60% of FSGS patients are steroid resistant; of these, 50-70% of patients will progress to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). African Americans have a genetic predisposition to FSGS and other kidney diseases (hypertensive nephropathy, lupus nephritis, HIV-associated nephropathy) due to allelic variants in the APOL1 gene (baseline allele: G0 variant; kidney disease risk variants in AAs: G1 and/or G2). APOL1 overexpression is toxic to mammalian cells; APOL1 risk variants have increased toxicity relative to G0 allele.Model for APOL1-associated kidney disease: kidney damage increases APOL1 expression in the glomerular podocytes; if APOL1 risk alleles are present, this induction causes podocyte cell death; podocyte death causes further kidney damage, contributing to further kidney disease.  Therapeutic concept: develop a small molecule inhibitor of APOL1-induced cell death to disrupt the cycle of APOL1-induced kidney damage.

TARGET_RATIONALE: MKNK1 (MNK1) is a MAP kinase-activated serine/threonine kinase that was identified as one of the strongest hits in a TRAIL modulators siRNA screen performed in-house using the T-ALL cell line, Jurkat. Additional in-house validation studies showed that MNK1 knockdown enhanced the sensitivity of AML (TF-1, ML-2, and K562) and multiple myeloma (L363) cell lines to apoptosis-inducing factors such as TRAIL and Fas ligand. From the analysis of MNK1/MNK2 double knockout mice it has been concluded that MNK1 and MNK2 expression is obligatory for the phosphorylation of eIF4E at serine residue 209. This site, conserved in humans, was initially believed to be necessary for cap-dependent translation, however, MNK1/MNK2 knockout mice develop normally in the absence of this phosphorylation. An exciting study published at the end of 2007 suggested that the regulation of eIF4E by MNK1 plays a critical role in oncogenesis. Specifically, c-myc overexpressing mouse hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) transduced with activated (but not kinase-dead) MNK1, or with eIF4E with an activating mutation (Ser-209-->Asp), elicited rapid lymphoma progression relative to HSCs expressing c-myc alone. It was also reported that  AML cells from patient bone marrow biopsies frequently express MNK1 protein, with expression levels correlating with the levels of c-myc. These studies, together with our original in-house validation data, support a model whereby MNK1 promotes resistance to apoptosis under conditions of oncogenic stress (e.g. c-myc expression). Through its regulation of eIF4E, MNK1 may selectively regulate a subset of genes involved in cell growth and survival, possibly at the level of cap-dependent translation initiation and/or by influencing mRNA transport. As evidenced for the latter model, phosphorylation of Ser209 in eIF4E by MNK1 was found to be important for the transport of cyclin-D1 and HDM2 mRNA from the nucleus to the cytoplasm. It should be emphasized that no apparent physical abnormalities were observed with the MNK1/MNK2 double knockout mice, consistent with the possibility of a favorable safety profile for MNK1 inhibitors (Ueda et. al., Mol. Cell. Biol. 24: 6539, 2004). Finally, structural (crystal) data have revealed attractive novel features of the MNK family kinase domain, including an enlarged kinase groove, an atypical open conformation, a zinc-binding site, and a DFD rather than DFG motif in the ATP-binding pocket.

TARGET_RATIONALE: ALS is a neuromuscular disorder characterized by the loss of neurons that innervate and control muscle. Loss of these motor neurons leads to progressive muscular weakness, paralysis and ultimately death due to respiratory failure. A treatment for ALS is urgently needed. Sphingolipids are structural membrane components that have bioactive roles in a number of processes affected by ALS including metabolism, myelination, neuroinflammation and pathways of cell death. Several lines of evidence suggest that accumulation of ceramide, the fundamental building block of all sphingolipid species, contributes to motor neuron degeneration. For example, partial loss of function mutations in the lysosomal enzyme acid ceramidase are associated with motor neuron disease. A reduction in acid ceramidase activity leads to the buildup of intracellular ceramide. In addition, we recently showed that disease progression in a transgenic mouse model of ALS was accelerated following administration of a compound that promotes ceramide accumulation (Dodge et al., PNAS 2015).  Follow up studies found that ceramide levels were elevated in the spinal cord of sporadic ALS patients and suggest that elevated ceramide levels were due in part to a pathological increase in de novo ceramide synthesis (rather than a decrease in acid ceramidase activity).  Interestingly, we also found a progressive increase in de novo ceramide synthesis in ALS mice (Dodge et al., unpublished). Serine palmitoyltransferase (SPTLC) is the rate-limiting enzyme that regulates de novo ceramide synthesis.  #  Hypothesis: Inhibition of SPTLC (de novo ceramide synthesis) will mitigate disease-associated elevations in ceramide and slow ALS disease progression

SPARC is a matricelullar protein involved in maturation of collagen fibers. The C3 domain is involved in the interaction between SPARC and collagens (Type I, III, IV). The C-terminal domain (or "Extracellular Calcium-binding", EC) of SPARC contains the 2 sites (RMRDWLKN & LIPME) which interact with the GVMGFO motif of the collagen III (col.III). SPARC function is to stabilize the col.III fibrillogenesis & is involved in tissue remodeling. Many studies show the expression of SPARC in damaged tissues & its involvement in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis & scleroderma: by blocking SPARC interaction with col.III with a mAb (but not the interaction of col.III with other ECM proteins, e.g., DDR2), it is expected to attenuate the fibrotic process in such diseases.

Vitamin D induces atherosclerosis in different animals fed a cholesterol rich diet. Vitamin D is activated in several consecutive steps in different organs (skin - liver -kidney). Recently it has been shown, that monocytes/macrophages have a strong capacity of vitamin D activation. The enzyme responsible therefor is CYP27B1.  We believe that the inhibition of CYP27B1-mediated vitamin D activation in monocytes/macrophages could protect people from the development of atherosclerosis.
